BURHAN:v1p253#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r2.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i counts four verses beginning with the letter shin and names them: “Month of Ramadan,” “God bears witness,” “grateful for His favor,” and “He prescribed for you of religion.”
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r2.anchor: وسئل الكسائى كم فى القرآن آية أولها شين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r1.claim: After mentioning particular favors, God mentions the general favor of a shared revealed religion: belief in divine unity, messengers, books, resurrection, and recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r1.anchor: لما عدد تعالى نعمه عليهم الخاصة، أتبعه بذكر نعمه العامة، وهو ما شرع لهم من العقائد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r2.claim: Abraham is singled out as the Arabs forebear, so they should follow his way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r2.anchor: أبا العرب، ففي ذلك هزلهم وبعث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r3.claim: Religions agree in these beliefs and many rulings, including prohibitions on adultery and unjust killing; it is said Noah first prohibited incestuous close kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r3.anchor: والشرائع متفقة فيما ذكرنا من العقائد، وفي كثير من الأحكام، كتحريم الزنا والقتل بغير حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses يجتبي as choosing; the following أن may be explanatory because the preceding wording carries the sense of speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r4.anchor: اختار، ويحتمل أن تكون أن مفسرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r5.claim: Alternatively أن is a verbal noun in accusative as substitute for ما, or in nominative as an explanation of the prescribed religion; إقامة الدين is God's unity and necessary beliefs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r5.anchor: فتكون في موضع نصب على البدل من ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r6.claim: The command forbids division because discord causes ruin, whereas unity and affection bring rescue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r6.anchor: ثم نهى عن التفرقة فيه، لأن التفرق سبب للهلاك، والاجتماع والألفة سبب للنجاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r7.claim: What seemed weighty and difficult to polytheists was God's unity, abandoning idols, and upholding the religion; divine choice consoles the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r7.anchor: ما توعدهم إليه من توحيد الله وترك عبادة الأصنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r8.claim: He says God chooses those who benefit from His enabling grace and kindness; Abū Ḥayyān flags this as Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328/r8.anchor: من يشاء: من ينفع فيهم توفيقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says Adam's sons had no formal duties or prohibited relations; Noah brought prohibitions on mothers and daughters and prescribed obligations, which later prophets reinforced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r1.anchor: لم يكن مع آدم عليه السلام إلا بنوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r2.claim: He describes one shared prophetic religion in fundamentals: monotheism, prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage, good works, truthfulness, trust, kinship, and bans on arrogance, adultery, harm, and cruelty to animals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r2.anchor: أوصيناك يا محمد ونوحا دينا واحدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r3.claim: The one religion persisted across prophets despite differences in their number; it is encapsulated by the call to uphold religion without division.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r3.anchor: فهذا كله مشروع دينا واحدا، أو ملة متحدة، لم يختلف على ألسنة الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says every prophet was commanded to uphold prayer, give alms, affirm God, and obey Him; this is what establishing the religion means.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r4.anchor: لم يبعث نبي إلا أمر بإقامة الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya defines establishing religion as sincerity toward God and worshipping Him, and says not to divide means not to become enemies over it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: إقامة الدين: الإخلاص لله وعبادته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r6.claim: Muqātil says not to divide means not to disagree, since each prophet confirms the others; another view says not to believe in some messengers while rejecting others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p328#2/r6.anchor: معناه لا تختلفوا، فإن كل نبي مصدق

STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r9.claim: The sūrah also treats the continuity between Islamic teaching and earlier religions.
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r9.anchor: The continuity between the teachings of Islam and previous religions is also addressed in v. 7 and vv. 13–15

TABATABAI:11:36-49#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#18/r3.claim: The named divine laws begin with Noah's; otherwise scripture would imply either an unmentioned separate law for others or neglect of them.
TABATABAI:11:36-49#18/r3.anchor: وأول ما ذكر من الشريعة هي شريعة نوح

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p118/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p118/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p118/r1.claim: Muhammad preached the same monotheistic religion as earlier prophets; idolaters and People of the Book opposed truth out of bias for invented religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p118/r1.anchor: all the earlier prophets were deputed to preach

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: For qualities such as goodness and ugliness, verbs commonly follow فعل يفعل and their verbal nouns take فعالة, فعالة, or فعل; adjectives often use فعيل, while حسن also uses فعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: فعالا وفعالة وفعلا وذلك قولك قبح يقبح قباحة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: نضر وجهه is intransitive and follows خرج يخرج; its adjectives ناضر and نضير and noun النضارة parallel forms already used for similar meanings.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقالوا نضر وجهه ينضر فبنوه على فعل يفعل مثل خرج يخرج لأن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Adjectives for appearance vary by lexical pattern: ضخم lacks the parallel ضخيم, while سبط and جعد have associated forms such as سباطة and سبوطة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: ضخم ولم يقولوا ضخيم كما قالوا عظيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Other bodily and evaluative traits show paired patterns: ملح/ملاحة/مليح, سمح/سماحة/سميح, and بهو/بهاء/جميل or شنع/شناعة/شنيع.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقالوا ملح ملاحة ومليح وسمح سماحة وسمح

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: أفعل adjectives may describe an inherent trait like color, as in أشنع; النظافة and الطهارة likewise have several noun and adjective patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقالوا أشنع فادخلوا أفعل في هذا إذ كان خصلة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Size and age adjectives such as عظيم, نبيل, صغير, and قديم have verbal nouns on فعالة as well as alternatives on فعل, فعلة, and فعولة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وما كان من الصغر والكبر فهو نحو من هذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: كثير and قليل are compared with adjectives of size: little parallels short, and the oppositions كثير/قليل and عظيم/صغير share patterns; طول is also an increase-and-decrease quality like قبح.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقد يقال للإنسان قليل كما يقال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: سمن and بطن form verbal nouns and adjectives like كبر and عظم, for example سمين and بطين.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقالوا سمن سمنا وهو سمين ككبر كبرا وهو كبير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Strength, bravery, weakness, and cowardice use several patterns: ضعيف, شجاعة/شجاع, جبان, وقور/وقارة, and جريء/جراءة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: ضعف ضعفا وهو ضعيف وقالوا شجع شجاعة وهو شجاع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: The chapter groups force and resistance traits together: قوي/قوة, سريع/سرعة, بطيء/بطء, ثقيل/ثقل, كميش/كماشة, حزن/حزونة, and صعب/صعوبة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وهو قوي كما قالوا سعد يسعد سعادة وهو سعيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Social rank and moral status show parallel patterns such as غني/غني, فقير/فقر, شريف/شرف, كريم/كرم, لئيم/لؤم, وضيع/ضعة, and رفيع.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: غني يغني غني وهو غني كما قالوا كبر يكبرا كبرا وهو كبير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: سعد/سعيد and شقي/شقي distinguish opposite states; رشد/راشد/رشيد and بخل/بخيل have multiple verbal-noun patterns, with reported comparisons differing by speaker.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: فأحدهما مرفوع والآخر موضوع وقالوا الشقاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Names for offices and companionship use forms such as أمير, وكيل, وصي, جليس, and عديل; the source relates these to ولاية and to the base عديل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وقالوا وكيل ووصي وجري كما قالوا أمير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Mental traits include حلم/حليم, علم/عالم/عليم, فقه/فقيه, لب/لبيب, فهم, and نقه; their verbal nouns and adjectives follow several established patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وما أتى من العقل فهو نحو من ذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: عقل is grouped with intransitive عجز because it does not pass beyond its agent; the passage also records رفق, حذق, لبق, and related forms for intelligence and skill.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: يعقل عقلا وهو عاقل كما قالوا عجز يعجز

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Further character terms include حصان for a chaste woman, like جبان, plus صلف and رقيع; حمق has several noun and adjective forms, including أحمق and أنوك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: وهي حصان كجبنت جبنا وهي جبان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.claim: Geminated roots tend to avoid فعلت and فعل because doubling with that pattern is heavy; ذل, شح, ضن, لب, قل, and عف illustrate alternative forms, and kasra is lighter than damma.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابايضافيالخصالالتيتكونفيال.anchor: فلما اجتمعا حادوا إلى غير ذلك وهو قولك ذل يذل ذلا

NAHHAS:v4p73/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r17.claim: Mā is the object of sharaʿa; alladhī is coordinated with it, and mā waṣṣaynā is also an object, meaning He prescribed for you.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r17.anchor: ما في موضع نصب بشرع ( والذي أوحينا إليك ) عطف عليها

NAHHAS:v4p73/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r18.claim: An aqīmū may be an accusative appositive to mā, a nominative clause with an omitted subject, or a genitive appositive to the pronoun.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r18.anchor: أن في موضع نصب على البدل من ما أي شرع لكم أن أقيموا الدين

NAHHAS:v4p73/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r19.claim: The prescription is to establish God's chosen religion and not divide by believing some messengers and rejecting others; the religion shared by the prophets is Islam.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r19.anchor: شرع لكم أن تقيموا لله الدين الذي ارتضاه ولا تتفرقوا فتؤمنوا ببعض الرسل وتكفروا ببعض

NAHHAS:v4p73/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r20.claim: Muhammad's community follows the prophets in this religion.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r20.anchor: فهذا الذي شرع لكم لجميع الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم أن يقيموا الدين الذي ارتضاه

NAHHAS:v4p73/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r21.claim: The Prophet's instruction to follow Abu Bakr and Umar means following their obedience to God's command and avoiding disobedience, not imitating them in every issue.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r21.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اقتدوا بالذين من بعدي أبي بكر وعمر أي اعملوا كما يعملان من اتباع أمر الله

NAHHAS:v4p73/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r22.claim: The imperative aqīmū can occur inside the relative clause because it means the infinitive, to establish the religion.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r22.anchor: جاز أن يكون أقيموا وهو أمر داخلا في الصلة لأن معناه كمعنى الفعل المضارع معناه أن تقيموا الدين

NAHHAS:v4p73/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r23.speaker: جماعة من أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v4p73/r23.claim: A group of exegetes say Noah was the first prophet to bring a revealed law, including prohibitions on close female relatives; al-Nahhas treats this as part of the preceding interpretation.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r23.anchor: ومذهب جماعة من أهل التفسير أن نوحا صلى الله عليه وسلم أول من جاء بالشريعة من تحريم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات

NAHHAS:v4p73/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r24.claim: What the Prophet calls them to is worship of God alone, which weighs heavily on the polytheists.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r24.anchor: أي من إقامة الدين لله جل وعز وحده

NAHHAS:v4p73/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r25.claim: The sense is that God chooses whoever He wishes to choose; the second verb is understood but omitted.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r25.anchor: أي من يشاء أن يجتبيه ثم حذف هذا

NAHHAS:v4p73/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p73/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p73/r26.claim: The ḍamma on yahdī is dropped because it is heavy, and yunību means to return or repent.
NAHHAS:v4p73/r26.anchor: حذفت الضمة من يهدي لثقلها وأناب رجع أي تاب

SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r1.claim: أن may be a verbal noun in the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject هو: the prescribed religion is God’s oneness.
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r1.anchor: أن تكون مصدرية في محل رفع على خبر ابتداء مضمر تقديره: هو أن أقيموا أي: الدين المشروع توحيد الله تعالى.

SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r2.claim: It may instead be accusative as a بدل from the relative phrase, effectively prescribing God’s oneness.
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r2.anchor: أنها في محل نصب بدلا من الموصول كأنه قيل: شرع لكم توحيد الله تعالى.

SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r3.claim: A third analysis makes it genitive as بدل from الدين.
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r3.anchor: أنها في محل جر بدلا من الدين.

SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r4.claim: A fourth analysis makes it genitive as بدل from the pronoun in به.
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r4.anchor: أنها في محل جر أيضا بدلا من الهاء.

SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r5.claim: It may be explanatory because it follows wording with the force of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:42:13/r5.anchor: أن تكون مفسرة؛ لأنها قد تقدمها ما هو بمعنى القول.

ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r5.claim: A tafsīr report says Noah was the first to prohibit marriage to daughters, sisters, and mothers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r5.anchor: روي في التفسير أن أول من أتى بتحريم البنات والأخوات والأمهات نوح

ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r6.claim: The wording means that God prescribed for the community what He prescribed for Abraham, Moses, and Jesus as well.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395/r6.anchor: أي وشرع لكم ما وصى به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r1.claim: أن can be accusative as the object or content of “He prescribed for you”: شرع لكم أن أقيموا الدين.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r1.anchor: فالنصب على معنى شرع لكم أن أقيموا الدين

ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r2.claim: أن can be nominative in an explanatory clause: هو أن أقيموا الدين.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r2.anchor: والرفع على معنى هو أن أقيموا الدين

ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r3.claim: أن can be genitive as an appositive to the preceding ب; Zajjāj calls this the least likely of the three parses.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r3.anchor: والجر على البدل من الباء، والجر أبعد هذه الوجوه،

ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, أن explicates what was prescribed to Noah, revealed to Muhammad, and prescribed to Abraham; the prescription to all is to establish religion and avoid division.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r4.anchor: وجائز أن يكون أن أقيموا الدين تفسيرا لما وصى به نوحا

ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r5.claim: The shared command to earlier peoples and this community is to uphold religion together and unite in following the messengers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p395#2/r5.anchor: فيكون المعنى: شرع لكم ولمن قبلكم إقامة الدين وترك الفرقة،

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r1.claim: Here din means religion's ethical and spiritual core, or faith generally, rather than religion including laws, which differed across dispensations.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r1.anchor: the term din cannot apply in this context to "religion" in its widest connotation, including religious laws

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r2.claim: The discourse returns to the unchanging spiritual and moral principles underlying all revealed religions.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n12/r2.anchor: the unchanging sameness of the spiritual and moral principles underlying all revealed religions.

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n13/r1.claim: The wording implies that Muhammad learned what God had enjoined on Noah only through revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n13/r1.anchor: Lit., "which We have revealed unto thee", implying that it was only through revelation that the Prophet Muhammad came to know

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r1.claim: Asad links the command to uphold faith with statements that self-surrender to God is the only true religion.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r1.anchor: Cf. 3:19 - "the only [true) religion in the sight of God is [man's) self-surrender unto Him"; and 3:85

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r2.claim: The command against division parallels the declarations that believers are one community under one Sustainer.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r2.anchor: Parallel with this principle, enunciated by all of God's apostles, is the categorical statement in 21:92 and 23:52

ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r3.speaker: Zamakhshari, Razi, Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r3.claim: Major commentators understand the verse as affirming ecumenical unity among monotheistic religions despite time-bound differences in their laws and practices.
ASAD-NOTES:42:12#n14/r3.anchor: Most of the great commentators (e.g., Zamakhshari, Razi, Ibn Kathir) understand this as an unequivocal reference to the ecumenical unity of all religions

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p7/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p7/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p7/r1.claim: The longer form “tatafarraqū” in the covenant spanning Noah through Muhammad presents the prohibition as enduring across nations and generations; Muslims are included in that universal injunction.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p7/r1.anchor: الوصية خالدة من زمن سيدنا نوح - عليه السلام - إلى خاتم الأنبياء - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فجاء الفعل (تتفرقوا)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r1.claim: The form تتفرقوا presents division as an enduring possibility across time, unlike the more bounded تفرقوا in the command specifically addressed to Muslims.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r1.anchor: وكذلك فالحدث ممتد في الأولى (تتفرقوا) والحدث محدد في الثانية (تفرقوا)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r2.claim: The command is a lasting prophetic covenant from Noah through Muhammad; the Muslim community is included in it and is separately addressed in 3:103, making the warning especially strong.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p458/r2.anchor: في الآية الأولى الوصية خالدة من زمن سيدنا نوح - عليه السلام - إلى خاتم الأنبياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p895/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p895/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p895/r2.claim: Al Imran addresses one Muslim community and forbids even a little division, using the shorter form; Shura addresses humanity across the prophets and uses the fuller form for the comprehensive scope.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p895/r2.anchor: فالكلام لكل البشر وذكر كل الأنبياء من زمن نوح إلى قيام الساعة فقال (تتفرقوا)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p907/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p907/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p907/r1.claim: The Qur'an uses awṣā for material matters such as inheritance and waṣṣā for spiritual matters such as the religion enjoined on the prophets.

GHARNATI:v1p182/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r1.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r1.claim: Muslims agree that the ordering of verses within each sūra was fixed by the Prophet's instruction and command.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r1.anchor: اعلم أولا أن ترتيب الآيات في سورها وقع بتوقيف - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأمره من غير خلاف في هذا بين المسلمين،

GHARNATI:v1p182/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r2.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r2.claim: The arrangement of suras in Uthman's official codex, copies of which he sent to the regions, was adopted by the Companions.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r2.anchor: وكما ثبت في الإمام مصحف عمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه الذي بعث بنسخة إلى الآفاق، وأطبقت الصحابة على موافقة عثمان في ترتيب سوره وعمله فيه،

GHARNATI:v1p182/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r3.speaker: مالك
GHARNATI:v1p182/r3.claim: Malik, Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib in his settled position, and most scholars hold that the Companions arranged the suras through ijtihad after the Prophet delegated the matter to the community.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r3.anchor: فذهب مالك، والقاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب. فيما اعتمده واستقر عليه مذهبه من قوليه، والجمهور من العلماء، إلى أن تريب السور إنما وقع باجتهاد الصحابة

GHARNATI:v1p182/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r4.speaker: طائفة من العلماء
GHARNATI:v1p182/r4.claim: Another group of scholars holds that the sura arrangement came through the Prophet's explicit instruction and command.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r4.anchor: وذهبت طائفة من العلماء إلى أن ذلك إنما وقع بتوقيفه عدوط وأمره

GHARNATI:v1p182/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r5.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r5.claim: Each side has evidence; neither position harms the religion, and both lead to certainty.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r5.anchor: ولكل من الطائفتين جهات تعلق، وكلا القولين والحمد لله لا يقدح في الدين، ولا يثمر إلا اليقين،

GHARNATI:v1p182/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r6.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r6.claim: Whatever account of the arrangement is adopted, it must observe correspondence, continuity, and affinity among suras.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r6.anchor: اعلم أن الأمر في ذلك كيفما قدر فلابد من رعي التناسب، والتفات التواصل والتجاذب،

GHARNATI:v1p182/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r7.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r7.claim: If the order came by Prophetic instruction, there is no basis for objection after that decisive delineation.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r7.anchor: فإن كان بتوقيف منه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، فلا مجال للخصم بعد ذلك التحديد الجليل والرسم،

GHARNATI:v1p182/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r8.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r8.claim: If the matter was delegated, the Companions exerted their utmost effort and were eminent in knowledge and understanding.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r8.anchor: وإن كان مما فوض فيه الأمر إلى الأمة بعده فقد أعمل الكل من الصحابة في ذلك جهده، وهم الأعلياء بعلمه، والمسلم لهم في وعيه وفهمه

GHARNATI:v1p182/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r9.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r9.claim: The Companions knew the occasions of revelation and the placement of the words, and compiled the Quran according to what they heard from the Messenger.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r9.anchor: والعارفون بأسباب نزول الآيات، ومواقع الكلمات، وإنما ألفوا القرآن على ما كانوا يسمعونه من رسول الله

GHARNATI:v1p182/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r10.speaker: مالك
GHARNATI:v1p182/r10.claim: Some transmit from Malik that the Companions arranged the Quran according to what they heard from the Messenger, although Malik is also named among those who held that sura order was their ijtihad.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r10.anchor: وهذا قول مالك ضي الله عنه في حكاية بعضهم عنه، ومالك أحد القائلين بأن ترتيب السور اجتهاد من المسلمين كما تقدم عنه

GHARNATI:v1p182/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r11.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r11.claim: In either account, the sura order was learned from the Prophet, and the Companions based their considered arrangement on what they had heard from him.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r11.anchor: فكيف مادار الأمر، فمنه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عرف ترتيب السور، وعلى ما سمعوه منه بنوا جليل ذلك النظر

GHARNATI:v1p182/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r12.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r12.claim: The real dispute is whether the order was established by explicit verbal instruction or by reliance on the Prophet's practice, which left room for Companions' reasoning.
GHARNATI:v1p182/r12.anchor: فإذا إنما الخلاف هل ذلك يتوقيف قولي أو بمجرد استناد فعلي بحيث بقى لهم فيه مجال للنظر؟ فهذا موضع الخلاف.

GHARNATI:v1p182/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p182/r13.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p182/r13.claim: He raises an objection: if the Companions heard the settled order from the Prophet, why did they exercise judgment, and what choice remained for them?
GHARNATI:v1p182/r13.anchor: فإن قيل إذا كانوا قد سمعوا منه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - استقر عليه ترتيبه ففيم إذا عملوا الأنظار، وأي مجال بقي لهم بعد للاختيار؟

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p125/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p125/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p125/r2.claim: The same monotheistic religion was preached from Noah through Jesus and Muḥammad, with the command to uphold it without division.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p125/r2.anchor: from Noah (sws) to Jesus (sws) every prophet has preached this very religion of monotheism and stopped people from creating differences in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p128/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p128/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p128/r4.claim: Addressing Quraysh and Arabia, Islahi explains that the religion revealed to Muhammad is the same one enjoined on Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus: every prophet, from the first to the final, preached God's true religion, so it is not novel or alien.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p128/r4.anchor: every prophet from the beginning to this final Prophet (sws) preached this very religion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r1.claim: The sequence names Noah and Muhammad first as the first and last prophets, then singles out Abraham, Moses and Jesus because pre-Qur’anic idolaters, Jews and Christians respectively claimed to follow them; it thus compresses prophetic history and highlights major communities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r1.anchor: at the beginning, the first and last of them – Noah (sws) and Muḥammad (sws) – are mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r2.claim: The definite article in al-dīn, like that in al-kitāb, means God's religion; Islahi cites 3:19, which says the true religion before God is Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r2.anchor: The religion of God has always been Islam as is mentioned in the following verse:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r3.claim: The religion's foundation is pure, complete monotheism, given to Noah and even Adam and revealed again to Muhammad; its beliefs and foundations remain the same, while differences lie only in sharīʿah's corollaries.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r3.anchor: The foundation of this religion is the pure and complete concept of monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r4.claim: Establishing religion requires sincere belief in its tenets and honest, righteous observance of its practical directives, with continuing care to prevent negligence and keep innovators from introducing changes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r4.anchor: To establish religion means to sincerely believe in tenets which are meant to be believed in

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r5.claim: The command against division presents religion as God's rope: everyone must cling to the true rope rather than accept another in its place, since breaking that bond leaves people with nothing to unite them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r5.anchor: if one’s relation with this rope of God is broken, then the binding thread will be torn apart

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r6.claim: The idolaters addressed as finding the call burdensome are the Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p129/r6.anchor: refers to the idolaters of the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r1.claim: Although the call is worded generally, context shows it means monotheism, the point Quraysh idolaters most strongly resisted throughout the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r1.anchor: contextual indications show that they relate to monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r2.claim: God's choosing assures the Prophet to be patient: His wise will and established practice prevail despite the Prophet's desire for their faith; He guides those who turn to Him, while others lose the urge for further guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r2.anchor: He guides only those to Himself who themselves turn to Him for guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r3.claim: The preposition ilā after the verb for choosing indicates taḍmīn, a construction Islahi says he has explained elsewhere in the exegesis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p130/r3.anchor: shows that a taḍmīn occurs here.

QIRAAT-ER:42:13:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:42:13:17#1/r1.speaker: canonical
QIRAAT-ER:42:13:17#1/r1.claim: The standard canonical reading retains accusative Ibrāhīma in the sequence of named recipients.
QIRAAT-ER:42:13:17#1/r1.anchor: canonical, mutawatir: Canonical standard line preserves accusative Ibrāhīma in the named recipient sequence

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p190#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p190#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p190#5/r1.claim: Qatada explains the prescribed religion as the rulings of what is lawful and unlawful.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p190#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ﴾ قال الحلال والحرام

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r1.claim: The prescription reflects God's perfect knowledge and wisdom; tracing it to the named prophets shows an ancient religion agreed upon by the messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r1.anchor: وإيذان بأنما شرع سبحانه لهم صادر عن كمال العلم والحكمة كما أن بيان نسبته إلى المذكورين عليهم الصلاة والسلام تنبيه على كونه دينا قديما

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r2.claim: The address is to Muhammad's community and refers to the religion prescribed to Noah and later law-bearing messengers and resolute, renowned prophets, with a reinforced command.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r2.anchor: والخطاب لأمته عليه الصلاة والسلام أيشرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ومن بعده من أرباب الشرائع وأولي العزم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r3.claim: These prophets are singled out for their rank and fame, and to draw unbelievers toward agreement: each group accepts a prophet, with Jews especially associated with Moses and Christians with Jesus.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r3.anchor: وتخصيص المذكورين بالذكر لما أشير إليه من علو شأنهم وعظم شهرتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r4.claim: Every prophet was commanded to establish Islam: affirm God's oneness and the enduring fundamentals of religious law and rulings that do not vary among peoples and ages.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r4.anchor: وإلا فما من نبي إلا وهو مأمور بما أمروا به من إقامة دين الإسلام وهو التوحيد وما لا يختلف باختلاف الأمم وتبدل الأعصار

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r5.claim: The word for enjoining signals the command's reinforcement and the care given to its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r5.anchor: كما ينبيء عنه التوصية فإنها معربة عن تأكيد الأمر والاعتناء بشأن المأمور به

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r6.claim: What was revealed to Muhammad may refer to the opening of this surah and 42:7, or more broadly to all revelations, including 16:123 and 18:110; Al-Alusi allows the broader reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r6.anchor: وإما ما يعمهما وغيرهما مما وقع في سائر المواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r7.claim: Using revelation here, instead of the surrounding language of enjoining, matches the cited verses and explicitly asserts Muhammad's messengership against deniers; the honorific shift signals special care for him and his revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r7.anchor: وإيثار الإيحاء على ما قبله وما بعده من التوصية لمراعاة ما وقع في الآيات المذكورة ولما في الإيحاء من التصريح برسالته

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r8.claim: The relative pronoun alladhi marks Muhammad's revealed law as receiving the greatest care, explaining why it precedes the later named prophets despite coming later in time.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك إشعار بأن شريعته ص هي الشريعة المعتنى بها غاية الاعتناء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r9.claim: Noah is mentioned first to state promptly that the prescribed religion is ancient; Noah is also said to have been the first messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r9.anchor: وتقديم توصية نوح عليه السلام للمسارعة إلى بيان كون المشروع لهم دينا قديما وقد قيل إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أول الرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r10.claim: Establishing the religion means maintaining Islam—God's oneness, obedience, belief in His books and messengers, the Day of Judgment, and all else that makes a servant a believer—and preserving its pillars from deviation while persevering in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r10.anchor: أي دين الإسلام الذي هو توحيد الله تعالى وطاعته والإيمان بكتبه ورسله وبيوم الجزاء وسائر ما يكون العبد به مؤمنا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r11.claim: An may be a verbal noun particle, or a lightened form of anna; the resulting verbal noun can be accusative as an appositive to the object of prescribed, or nominative as the predicate or subject of an elliptical clause answering the ambiguity about what was prescribed.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p20#3/r11.anchor: و ( أن ) مصدرية وتقدم الكلام في وصلها بالأمر والنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r1.claim: The clause can explain the preceding wording because it implies speech without an explicit saying verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r1.anchor: ما يتضمن معنى القول دون حروفه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r2.claim: Another parse makes it a genitive substitute for the pronoun in ‘what He enjoined’; the relative clause retains a referent because the replaced element is conceptually omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r2.anchor: على أنه بدل من ضمير ( به ) ولا يلزمه بقاء الموصول بلا عائد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r3.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r3.claim: Sheikh al-Islam objects that this parsing removes the command from revelation to Muhammad and implies the prohibition addresses earlier prophets, though it is intended for Muhammad’s community.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r3.anchor: مع إفاضته إلى خروجه عن حيز الأيحاء إلى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r4.claim: The clause may instead be a substitute for the word ‘religion.’
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r4.anchor: وجوز كونه بدلا من ( الدين ) ويجوز كون ( أن ) مفسره

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r5.speaker: غير واحد من الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r5.claim: Several eminent scholars take the command and prohibition to address Muhammad and his followers as well as earlier prophets and their communities.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r5.anchor: على ما اختاره غير واحد من الأجلة شامل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأتباعه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r6.claim: Alusi finds the prohibition most plausibly addressed to Muhammad’s community, the people who became divided; addressing earlier prophets’ communities would be strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r6.anchor: وأنهم المتفرقون ثم بين ما استظهره وسنشير إليه إن شاء الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r7.claim: Religion here means the shared fundamentals; the prohibition is against accepting some and rejecting others, not differing over subsidiary laws that varied between communities.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r7.anchor: الذي هو عبارة عما تقدم من الأصول بأن يأتي به بعض ولا يأتي بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r8.claim: Some include certain subsidiary matters among the fundamentals intended by ‘religion’ here.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r8.anchor: وبعضهم أدخل بعض الفروع في أصول الدين المرادة هنا من الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r9.claim: Mujahid says every prophet was commanded to establish prayer, give alms, affirm God, and obey Him; these make up establishing religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد : لم يبعث نبي إلا أمر بأقامة الصلاة وأيتاء الزكاة والإقرار بالله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r10.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r10.claim: Ibn al-Arabi describes religious prescriptions developing from Adam’s basic guidance, through Noah’s prohibitions and duties, then being reinforced by successive prophets until the final law.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r10.anchor: وقال الحافظ أبو بكر بن العربي : لم يكن مع آدم عليه السلام إلا بنوه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r11.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the prophets shared one religion in fundamentals, including worship, moral virtues, trustworthiness, kinship, and avoiding arrogance, adultery, cruelty, and disgraceful conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r11.anchor: فمعنى الآية شرعنا لكم ماشرعنا للأنبياء دينا واحدا في الأصول وهي التوحيد والصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r12.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi glosses establishing religion as making it endure continuously, without disagreement or instability.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r12.anchor: اجعلوه قائما أي دائما مستمرا من غير خلاف فيه ولا اضطراب انتهى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r13.claim: Alusi qualifies Ibn al-Arabi’s list: prayer, alms, fasting, and pilgrimage must mean these rites generically, since their specific forms belong to Muhammad’s community and the sura is Meccan.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r13.anchor: ولعله أراد بالصلاة والزكاة والصيام والحج مطلقا لا ما نعرفه منها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r14.claim: Religions certainly differed in subsidiary laws; specific alms and Ramadan fasting were instituted in Medina, and pilgrimage apparently was not prescribed for Moses’ and Jesus’ communities or most earlier peoples.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r14.anchor: وبالجملة لا شك في اختلاف الأديان في الفروع نعم لا يبعد اتفاقها فيما هو من مكارم الأخلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r15.claim: What grievously burdens the polytheists is the Prophet’s continuing call to monotheism and rejection of idols, the foremost principle and their greatest difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r15.anchor: على سبيل الأستمرار التجددي من التوحيد ورفض عبادة الأصنام ويشعر بإرادته التعبير

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r16.claim: Another possible referent is the call to establish religion and avoid division.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r16.anchor: أو ما تدعوهم إليه من إقامة الدين وعدم التفرق فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r17.claim: God’s choosing and guiding those who turn to Him consoles the Prophet: some among those called will respond.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p21/r17.anchor: تسلية له صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن منهم من تجنب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r1.claim: Alusi prefers both pronouns ‘to Him’ to refer to God: He selects through divine grace and guides through direction and enabling those who turn to Him; the chosen and guided are distinct groups within the people of religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r1.anchor: قال في الكشف أظهر وأملأ بالفائدة أما الثاني فللدلالة على أن أهل الاجتباء غير أهل الاهتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r2.claim: Some refer both pronouns to religion, understanding ‘choose’ as gathering people to faith, which suits the preceding mention of division.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r2.anchor: ومنهم من اختار جعله للدين لمناسبة معنوية هي اتحاد المتفرق فيه والمجتمع عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives ‘choose’ from gathering and refers the pronoun to religion; Alusi calls this a surface-level reading based on the preceding theme of unity.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r3.anchor: والزمخشري اختار كونه من الجباية بمعنى الجمع وعود الضمير على الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r4.claim: The verb ‘choose’ is more commonly used for selection, making the people of religion God’s elect, chosen for Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r4.anchor: فلأن الاجتباء بمعنى الاصطفاء أكثر استعمالا ولأنه يدل أن أهل الدين هم صفوة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r5.claim: Another reading takes the call as belief in the prophetic message: the polytheists resent the Prophet’s selection for revelation, and God’s choice answers them as in ‘God knows best where to place His message.’
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r5.anchor: على معنى ما تدعوهم إلى الإيمان به والمراد به الرسالة أي ثقلت عليهم رسالتك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p22/r6.claim: Alusi prefers the earlier explanation of the call as monotheism and establishing religion over the alternative focused on the Prophet’s appointment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r4.claim: To prescribe the religion means to explain and establish it as a law for you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r4.anchor: {شرع لكم من الدين} بين وسن لكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r5.claim: Noah was the first prophet given a revealed law.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r5.anchor: {ما وصى به نوحا} وهو أول أنبياء الشريعة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r6.claim: Mujahid says God prescribed one religion to Muhammad and Noah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: أوصيناك وإياه يا محمد دينا واحدا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r7.claim: What was revealed to Muhammad means the Quran and the laws of Islam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r7.anchor: {والذي أوحينا إليك} من القرآن وشرائع الإسلام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r8.claim: Qatada says the shared religion consists of declaring lawful what God permits and forbidden what He prohibits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r8.anchor: فقال قتادة: تحليل الحلال وتحريم الحرام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r9.speaker: الحكم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r9.claim: Al-Hakam identifies the shared prescription as forbidding marriage to mothers, daughters, and sisters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r9.anchor: وقال الحكم: تحريم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r10.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r10.claim: Mujahid says every prophet was charged with prayer, almsgiving, and acknowledging obedience to God; this is the religion prescribed to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لم يبعث الله نبيا إلا وصاه بإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والإقرار لله بالطاعة له،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r11.claim: Another view identifies the shared religion as affirming God's oneness and disavowing association with Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو التوحيد والبراءة من الشرك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r12.claim: Another view takes the prescription to be the following command: all prophets were sent to establish religion and unity, and to leave division and disagreement.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p186#3/r12.anchor: وقيل: هو ما ذكر من بعد، وهو قوله: {أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه} بعث الله الأنبياء كلهم بإقامة الدين والألفة والجماعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r1.claim: What Muhammad calls the polytheists to—affirming God's oneness and rejecting idols—is grievous to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r1.anchor: كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه} من التوحيد ورفض الأوثان ثم قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r2.claim: God chooses and selects whichever of His servants He wills to draw near to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r2.anchor: الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء} يصطفي إليه (2) من عباده من يشاء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r3.claim: God guides to Himself whoever turns toward obedience to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p187/r3.anchor: ويهدي إليه من ينيب} يقبل إلى طاعته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r4.claim: God prescribed the shared religion of Noah, Muhammad, and the other law-bearing prophets.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r4.anchor: أي شرع لكم من الدين دين نوح ومحمد عليهما الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r5.claim: The common foundation is establishing religion through required belief and obedience to God’s rulings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r5.anchor: وهو الأصل المشترك فيما بينهم المفسر بقوله: { أن أقيموا الدين }

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r6.claim: The clause may be accusative as apposition to the object of “prescribed,” nominative as an independent answer, or genitive as apposition to the pronoun in به.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r6.anchor: ومحله النصب على البدل من مفعول { شرع } ، أو الرفع على الاستئناف

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r7.claim: Communities must not divide over this shared foundation, though branches of law differ, as 5:48 says.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r7.anchor: ولا تختلفوا في هذا الأصل أما فروع الشرائع مختلفة كما قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r8.claim: The Prophet’s call to monotheism is grievous to polytheists.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r9.claim: Yajtabī means God draws people to Him; the pronoun refers to the call or religion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r9.anchor: يجتلب إليه والضمير لما تدعوهم أو للدين

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:12-13/r10.claim: God guides by indication and enabling those who turn to Him.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r3.claim: Since God alone governs existence, He alone lays down the paths of religion, the greatest provision; He legislated the shared religion upheld by the prophets.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r3.anchor: وأنه لا متصرف في الوجود سواه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r4.claim: “He legislated” means He laid down a clear, manifest path for the final community.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r4.anchor: أي طرق وسن طريقا ظاهرا بينا واضحا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r5.claim: Religion here is what people practice and are recompensed for.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r6.claim: Noah is named first as the earliest messenger forefather sent to dissenters; the same religion runs from him through the final Prophet and intervening famous prophets.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r6.anchor: ذكر لهم أول الآباء المرسلين إلى المخالفين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r7.claim: If the Arabs reject the religion as new, Biqāʿī argues it is actually the oldest; every prophet came with it and innate human nature bears witness, even in hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r7.anchor: فإن كنتم إنما تأنفون من الدخول في هذا الدين لحدوثه فإنه أقدم الأديان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r8.claim: The Qur’anic revelation to Muhammad is singled out with “We revealed” and placed before earlier prophets; its full meaning is uniquely grasped by him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r8.anchor: أبرزه في مظهر العظمة معبرا بالوحي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r9.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes Muhammad’s revelation from the others’ enjoinment, presenting it as greater; he also marks Abraham’s honor through the majestic plural.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r9.anchor: ودل على عظمه ما كان لإبراهيم وبنيه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r10.claim: Abraham was saved from Nimrod’s plot and fire and given Ishmael and Isaac in old age; as a leading ancestor of the Arabs, he should be followed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r10.anchor: نجيناه من كيد نمرود بالنار وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r11.claim: Moses received the Torah as admonition and an explanation of everything.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r11.anchor: أنزلنا عليه التوراة موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r12.claim: Jesus received the Gospel containing guidance, light, and admonition; God preserved him in heaven for the law of the final Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p609/r12.anchor: ودخرناه في سمائنا شريعة الخاتم الفاتح

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r1.claim: “That you establish the religion” may substitute for the object of “He legislated,” or begin a new sentence; “that” may be a verbal noun or explanatory after wording that implies speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r1.anchor: أبرزه في أسلوب الأمر فقال مبدلا من معمول

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r2.claim: All final and earlier communities are commanded to establish the religion: return to primordial monotheism, affirm every perfection of God, and uphold what His messengers conveyed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r2.anchor: بالرجوع إلى ما فطروا عليه وقت الاضطرار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r3.claim: The added tāʾ in the prohibition signals emphatic, grave division; Biqāʿī suggests warning against division in fundamentals while allowing some subsidiary interpretation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r3.anchor: تفرقا عظيما بما أشار إليه إثبات التاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r4.claim: Communities should preserve unity in ease as well as hardship; division brings ruin, unity brings deliverance, so the People of the Book should be one hand.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r4.anchor: النداة , فكونوا يدا واحدة يا أهل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r5.claim: Biqāʿī reinforces unity by quoting the call to the People of the Book to agree on a common word: worship God alone and take no lords besides Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r5.anchor: يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r6.claim: The call to unite on God’s oneness weighs heavily on the polytheists and constricts their chests, so they seek to divide believers; division sides with the envious enemy against God.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r7.claim: Although polytheists resist the call, God can bring anyone He wills into the religion; the shift to God’s name emphasizes His power over every heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r7.anchor: كيف السبيل مع ذلك إلى دخول أحد في هذا الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r8.claim: “Chooses” means selecting with utmost care and drawing the chosen person toward the religion.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r9.claim: God guides the one who turns back by enabling obedience; such a person is ready to renew inward return to obedience at every moment while progressing through its stations.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p610/r9.anchor: بالتوفيق للطاعة { من ينيب * } أي فيه أهلية

DURR-FULL:v7p339/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r4.claim: Mujāhid says God prescribed one religion to Muḥammad and all prophets, as He did to Noah.
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} : قال: وصاك يا محمد وأنبياءه كلهم دينا واحدا

DURR-FULL:v7p339/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses the prescribed religion as its lawful and forbidden matters.
DURR-FULL:v7p339/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} قال: الحلال والحرام

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r1.speaker: زيد بن رفيع
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r1.claim: Zayd says the religion prescribed to Noah, Moses, and Jesus endured until heresy extinguished it; he fears heresy will ruin this religion.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن رفيع بقية أهل الجزيرة قال: بعث الله نوحا عليه السلام وشرع له الدين فكان الناس في شريعة نوح

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r2.speaker: الحكم
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r2.claim: Al-Ḥakam says Noah's law prohibited marriage to mothers, sisters, and daughters.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r2.anchor: عن الحكم قال: {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} قال: جاء نوح عليه السلام بالشريعة بتحريم الأمهات

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses establishing religion as acting according to it.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r3.anchor: عن السدي - رضي الله عنه {أن أقيموا الدين} قال: اعملوا به

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r4.claim: Qatāda calls division ruinous and community cohesion a source of trust.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: {أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه} قال: تعلموا أن الفرقة هلكة وأن الجماعة ثقة

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r5.claim: Qatāda says polytheists found monotheism burdensome; Satan opposed it but God made it prevail.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r5.anchor: قال: استكبر المشركون أن قيل لهم: لا إله إلا الله ضانها إبليس وجنوده ليردوها فأبى الله إلا أن يمضيها

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r6.claim: Mujāhid says God singles out for Himself whomever He wills.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - {الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء} قال: يخلص لنفسه من يشاء

DURR-FULL:v7p340/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r8.claim: Al-Suddī glosses those turning back as people turning to obedience and identifies later scriptural inheritors as Jews and Christians.
DURR-FULL:v7p340/r8.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ويهدي إليه من ينيب} قال: من يقبل إلى طاعة الله وفي قوله {وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم} قال: اليهود والنصارى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r2.claim: The passage moves from bodily blessings to the spiritual blessing of Islam, addressing the Messenger and believers to honor the religion while indirectly censuring the unbelievers who reject it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r2.anchor: انتقال من الامتنان بالنعم الجثمانية إلى الامتنان بالنعمة الروحية بطريق الإقبال على خطاب الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r3.claim: “He legislated” means He clarified the paths of what He charged them with; the root denotes making a broad path, then came to mean establishing laws and religions, a metaphor for clarification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r3.anchor: أوضح وبين لكم مسالك ما كلفكم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r4.claim: “The religion” is a generic definite noun covering the earlier divinely revealed religions, while “from” is partitive.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r5.claim: A recommendation is a command coupled with exhortation; Islam is a religion like the one Noah was commanded and urged to follow, expressed either with an omitted “like” or an implicit simile treated as identity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r5.anchor: الأمر بشيء مع تحريض على إيقاعه والعمل به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r6.claim: The construction can be understood as “the same as what Noah was charged with”; this kind of compressed comparison is common, illustrated by Waraqa ibn Nawfal’s phrase about the revelation sent to Jesus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r6.anchor: هذا هو الناموس الذي أنزل على عيسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r7.claim: The religions match in core divine attributes, monotheism, the five necessities, and further needs required for human order; each earlier religion’s equivalent is present in Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r7.anchor: المماثلة في أصول الدين مما يجب لله تعالى من الصفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p49/r8.claim: Earlier religions taught monotheism, belief in resurrection and the afterlife, general piety, obedience, avoidance of prohibitions, and customary virtues; their details and branches differed, as the earlier scriptures confirm.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r1.claim: Islam preserves the shared fundamentals while differing from earlier religions in the scope of particular branches; this law also distinguishes itself through reasoned rulings, blocking harmful means, evidence-based inquiry, removing hardship, leniency, and close fit with human nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r1.anchor: ودين الإسلام لم يخل عن تلك الأصول وإن خالفها في التفاريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r2.claim: Alternatively, if “that” is explanatory, the resemblance concerns the following command: every messenger was charged to establish the revealed religion and avoid division; either way, Islam continues the earlier religions’ good in this life and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r2.anchor: أو المراد المماثلة فيما وقع عقبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r3.claim: Noah is named because he was the first messenger sent to humanity, so his religion is the foundation of the religions; the author links this sequence with 4:163.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r3.anchor: لأن نوحا أول رسول أرسله الله إلى الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r4.claim: Abraham’s religion is the root of ḥanīfism, spread among Arabs through Ishmael, and remained familiar through pilgrimage, circumcision, hospitality, and chivalry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r4.anchor: ولأن دين إبراهيم هو أصل الحنيفية وانتشر بين العرب بدعوة إسماعيل إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r5.claim: Moses is included because his religion had the broadest body of legal rulings among earlier religions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r5.anchor: ودين موسى هو أوسع الأديان السابقة في تشريع الأحكام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r6.claim: Jesus is included because his religion immediately preceded Islam, with no other religion between them, and because the sequence prepares Jews and Christians to be invited to Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r6.anchor: وأما دين عيسى فلأنه الدين الذي سبق دين الإسلام ولم يكن بينهما دين آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r7.claim: Placing Muhammad’s revelation after Noah’s pairs the first and final religions to signal Islam’s finality, then places the three intervening religions between them as a deliberate arrangement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r7.anchor: وتعقيب ذكر دين نوح بما أوحي إلى محمد عليهما السلام للإشارة إلى أن دين الإسلام هو الخاتم للأديان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r8.claim: Without this ordering rationale, Islam would have been mentioned first, as it is in 4:163 and 33:7.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p50/r8.anchor: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيئين من بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r1.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that Muhammad is placed first in the covenant list in 33:7 to show his superiority, since that passage enumerates those bound by the covenant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r1.anchor: الكشاف } في آية الأحزاب أن تقديم ذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r2.claim: Here the order instead presents Islam as the original, upright religion sent first through Noah and finally through Muhammad, with the other named religions between them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r2.anchor: وأما آية سورة الشورى فإنما أوردت في مقام وصف دين الإسلام بالأصالة والاستقامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r3.claim: “What We revealed to you” is the Qur’an already revealed before this verse, including its rulings; it is coordinated with Noah’s charge because it adds detailed elaboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r3.anchor: هو ما سبق نزوله قبل هذه الآية من القرآن بما فيه من أحكام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r4.claim: Avoiding three consecutive instances of the same relative form could explain the variation, but the author favors a subtle semantic distinction between the forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r4.anchor: وقد يظهر في بادىء الرأي أنه مجرد تفنن بتجنب تكرير الكلمة ثلاث مرات متواليات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r5.claim: Al-ladhī is the definite relative form identifying something known through its clause; mā began as a general, ambiguous noun needing a description, then often functioned as a relative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r5.anchor: وأخواته هي الأصل في الموصولات فهي موضوعة من أصل الوضع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r6.speaker: الزمخشري وجماعة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and others parse the mā in “God’s excellent counsel” as an indefinite “thing,” described by the following clause.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r7.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r7.claim: Sībawayh reads mā in “this is what is ready with me” as “a thing”; the following anonymous poetic line likewise uses mā for something beneficial, with “beneficial” qualifying it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r7.anchor: وقال سيبويه في قوله تعالى : هذا ما لدي عتيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r8.claim: Mā suits the old laws, no longer known except in general terms, while al-ladhī suits Muhammad’s familiar, current law; the author suggests this may be an overlooked subtlety of Qur’anic inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r8.anchor: لمناسبة أنها شرائع بعد العهد بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r9.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural in “what We revealed to you” is iltifāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r9.anchor: وفي العدول من الغيبة إلى التكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r10.claim: The quoted anonymous poem uses mā for “a thing” and the adjective “beneficial” to describe it, illustrating the original indefinite sense of the relative form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p51/r10.anchor: لما نافعع يسعى اللبيب فلا تكن لشيء بعيد نفعه الدهر ساعيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r1.claim: The four earlier laws are described with “charged” while Muhammad’s is “revealed” because the former were temporary, awaiting a later law, like a trust held until its owner arrives; the wording also echoes 42:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r1.anchor: وفي جانب شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل الإيحاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r2.claim: “That you establish the religion” may be a verbal noun clause functioning as an appositive to the first or final mā; coordination makes it apply equally to all the charges under “He legislated.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r2.anchor: مصدرية ، فإنها قد تدخل على الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r3.claim: Alternatively, “that” may explain “charged,” which implies speech: God charged every named messenger to establish the religion and unite around it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r3.anchor: لأنه يتضمن معنى القول دون حروفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r4.claim: On the explanatory reading, earlier religions shared the obligation to maintain their revealed religion, while the broad command is specified by each religion’s own branches.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه يقتضي أن ما حكي شرعه في الأديان السابقة هو هذا المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r5.claim: Establishing something means making it stand; here it is a metaphor for taking care to practice it, as in the phrase “they establish prayer.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r5.anchor: وهي استعارة للحرص على العمل به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r6.claim: The imperative “establish” addresses the communities of the named messengers, though their communities were not mentioned explicitly; the command to convey implies them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r6.anchor: أمم أولئك الرسل ولم يسبق لهم ذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r7.claim: The prohibition against division follows the command to establish the religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r7.anchor: وأعقب الأمر بإقامة الدين بالنهي عن التفرق في الدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r8.claim: Division is the opposite of gathering; originally it means bodies moving apart, and by metaphor it describes strong differences in circumstances and opinions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r8.anchor: تباعد الذوات ، أي اتساع المسافة بينها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r9.claim: The prohibition covers communities splitting over belief in or rejection of their messengers, and believers forming sects over religion’s principles, rules, or aims, which can disable and undermine its foundations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p52/r9.anchor: ويشمل التفرق بين الذين آمنوا بأن يكونوا نحلا وأحزابا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r1.claim: The prohibition means not to divide over carrying out the religion, with some working to establish it while others hold back; agreement channels and strengthens effort, as each member helps the rest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r1.anchor: ولا تتفرقوا في إقامته بأن ينشط بعضهم لإقامته ويتخاذل البعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r2.claim: Division wastes religious affairs and breeds enmity that can lead people to plot against one another; the Qur’an similarly warns that disputation brings failure and loss of strength.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r2.anchor: أما إذا حصل التفرق والاختلاف فذلك مفضض إلى ضياع أمور الدين في خلال ذلك الاختلاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r3.claim: The Prophet says that when God wants good for someone, He grants that person understanding of religion; differences in legal branches based on scholars’ reasoning count as such religious learning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r3.anchor: وأما الاختلاف في فروعه بحسب استنباط أهل العلم بالدين فذلك من التفقه الوارد فيه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r4.claim: The statement about Islam being difficult for the polytheists interrupts the connection between legislating religion and the following account of their division; it also answers why they rejected a religion supported by prior revelations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r4.anchor: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r5.claim: “It was hard” means difficult, like “heavy”: they could not accept the call. It metaphorically describes what the soul finds unwelcoming, and “upon” reflects the included sense of weight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r5.anchor: عجزوا عن قبول ما تدعوهم إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r6.claim: The indefinite relative “what” presents the Islamic call as something the polytheists denied, found strange, and considered impossible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r6.anchor: اعتبارا بنكران المشركين لهذه الدعوة واستغرابهم إياها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p54/r7.claim: One reason the call seemed difficult was its messenger: they objected that he was a human like them and not one of the leading men from the two towns.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r1.claim: A second objection concerned revelation’s form: the polytheists expected a book sent down all at once and demanded one, angels, sight of God, or direct speech from Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r1.anchor: وجهة ما به الدعوة فإنهم حسبوا أن الله لا يخاطب الرسل إلا بكتاب ينزله إليه دفعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r2.claim: A third objection was the message’s substance, which opposed their desires: they protested against one God and mocked the prospect of being created anew after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r2.anchor: ومن جهة ما تضمنته الدعوة مما لم تساعد أهواؤهم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r3.claim: The present-tense verb indicates that the Prophet’s invitation was renewed and continued over time.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r4.claim: This explanatory resumption answers why Islam’s call seemed difficult: God selects whom He wills, so the polytheists were not selected or destined for guidance because they remained distant from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r4.anchor: استئناف بياني جواب عن سؤال من يسأل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r5.claim: Alternatively, the statement rebuts a claim underlying their denial of the Messenger: God chooses whom He wills and need not follow their conventions about social rank or leadership.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ردا على إحدى شبههم الباعثة على إنكارهم رسالته بأن الله يجتبي من يشاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r6.claim: Ijtibāʾ means drawing near and choosing; God chooses those He guides to His religion from among those who turn to Him, and knows the inward secrets of creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r6.anchor: ومن يشاء الله اجتباءه من هداه إلى دينه ممن ينيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r7.speaker: author
