IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r7.claim: Fronting the divine subject before the verbal predicate implies exclusivity, answering those who denied that God would send a human and judged the weak believers inferior to themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p55/r7.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه وهو اسم الجلالة على الخبر الفعلي لإفادة القصر ردا على المشركين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r1.claim: God prescribed and clarified beliefs and monotheism of the kind He had enjoined on Noah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r1.anchor: المعنى: شرع لكم وبين من المعتقدات والتوحيد ما وصى به نوحا قبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r2.claim: Wa-alladhī coordinates with mā; the instruction to establish religion is likewise part of the prescribed teaching shared across the prophetic missions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r2.anchor: وقوله: والذي عطف على ما، وكذلك ما ذكر بعد من إقامة الدين مشروع اتفقت النبوات فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r3.claim: The verse can mean that the law given Muḥammad resembles those of Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus in shared beliefs and in containing rulings, since every prophetic mission includes both.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r3.anchor: فيجيء المعنى على هذا: شرع لكم شرعة هي كشرعة نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى عليهم السلام في أنها ذات المعتقدات المشهورة التي هي في كل نبوءة وذات أحكام كما كانت تلك كلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Qatāda's explanation that what Noah was charged with means the lawful and unlawful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يتخرج ما حكاه الطبري عن قتادة قال: ما وصى به نوحا يريد الحلال والحرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r5.speaker: نوح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r5.claim: A report says Noah was the first to prohibit marrying daughters and mothers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r5.anchor: وعليه روي أن نوحا أول من أتى بتحريم البنات والأمهات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r6.claim: Specific rulings differ among the prophetic laws, as expressed in 5:48.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r6.anchor: وأما الأحكام بانفرادها فهي في الشرائع مختلفة، وهي المراد في قوله تعالى: لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r7.claim: The clause an aqīmū can be accusative as an apposition to mā, genitive as an apposition to the pronoun in bihi, nominative as the predicate of an implied dhālika, or explanatory with no syntactic case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r7.anchor: وأن في قوله: أن أقيموا يجوز أن تكون في موضع نصب بدلا من ما، ويجوز في موضع خفض بدلا من الضمير في به، وفي موضع رفع على خبر ابتداء تقديره: ذلك أن، وأن تكون مفسرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r8.claim: Establishing the religion means worshiping God alone and rejecting all others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r8.anchor: وإقامة الدين هو توحيد الله تعالى ورفض سواه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r9.claim: The command forbids destructive division into tendencies and sects; goodness lies in concord and unity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r9.anchor: وقوله: ولا تفرقوا نهي عن المهلك من تفرق الأنحاء والمذاهب، والخير كله في الإلفة واجتماع الكلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r10.claim: The call to establish the religion was difficult for the polytheists who worshiped idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r10.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى نبيه بصعوبة موقع هذه الدعوة إلى إقامة الدين على المشركين بالله العابدين الأصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r11.claim: Qatāda says lā ilāha illā Allāh was hard for the polytheists, but God insisted on supporting it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r11.anchor: قال قتادة: كبرت عليهم: لا إله إلا الله، وأبى الله إلا نصرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r12.claim: Yajtabī means to choose and select; Mujāhid and others explain yunību as turning back from unbelief, seeking and desiring good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29/r12.anchor: ثم سلاه عنهم بقوله: الله يجتبي أي يختار ويصطفي، قاله مجاهد وغيره: و: ينيب معناه يرجع عن الكفر ويحرص على الخير ويطلبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.claim: The prohibition addresses Arab polytheists, Jews, Christians, and everyone called to Islam; the following account of division refers to the early Jews and Christians.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: ولا تتفرقوا عبارة يجمع خطابها كفار العرب واليهود والنصارى وكل مدعو إلى الإسلام، فلذلك حسن أن يقال: ما تفرقوا، يعني بذلك أوائل اليهود والنصارى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r1.claim: Shara'a means to explain and make clear.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the religion prescribed to Noah comprised permitting the lawful and forbidding the unlawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r2.anchor: أنه تحليل الحلال وتحريم الحرام قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r3.speaker: الحكم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r3.claim: Al-Hakam says the prescription to Noah was the prohibition of sisters and mothers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r4.claim: A third reported view identifies Noah's prescription as monotheism and abandoning shirk; no authority is named for it here.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r5.claim: What was revealed to Muhammad refers to the Quran and the laws of Islam.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the syntax by supplying “He prescribed” for what was revealed to Muhammad and what was prescribed to Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى وشرع الذي أوحينا إليك وشرع لكم ما وصى به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r7.claim: “Establish the religion” explains what God prescribed to Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r7.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أن أقيموا الدين ﴾ تفسير قوله ﴿ وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may explain all three prescriptions, making establishment of religion, avoidance of division, and unity in following the messengers a shared command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r8.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تفسيرا لما وصى به نوحا ولقوله ﴿ والذي أوحينا إليك ﴾ ولقوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r9.claim: Muqatil says establishing the religion means affirming God's oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل ﴿ أن أقيموا الدين ﴾ يعني التوحيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r10.claim: The command not to divide means not to differ in religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r10.anchor: ﴿ ولا تتفرقوا فيه ﴾ أي لا تختلفوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p276#2/r11.claim: The message weighs heavily on the polytheists of Mecca.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p277/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p277/r1.claim: God selects from His servants whomever He wills for His religion and guides to it whoever turns back to His obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p277/r1.anchor: أي يصطفي من عباده لدينه ﴿ من يشاء ويهدي ﴾ إلى دينه ﴿ من ينيب ﴾ أي يرجع إلى طاعته

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r1.claim: Sharaʿa means to institute a clear path; God instituted for Muhammad's community monotheism, Islam, and the foundations of religious laws and rulings.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r1.anchor: شرع بمعنى سن وجعل سنة وطريقا واضحا ؛ أي : سن الله لكم يا أمة محمد

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r2.claim: Tawṣiya is a strongly emphasized command given with admonition.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r2.anchor: والوصية : التقدم إلى الغير بما يعمل به مقترنا بوعظه ؛ أي : أمر به نوحا أمرا مؤكدا

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r3.claim: Noah is named first because he was the first prophet given a revealed law with lawful and forbidden matters, including prohibitions on close relatives that remain in force.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r3.anchor: قدم نوح عليه السلام ؛ لأنه أول أنبياء الشريعة ؛ فإنه أول من أوحي إليه الحلال والحرام

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r4.claim: What was revealed to Muhammad is the same law instituted for the community.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r4.anchor: {والذي أوحينا إليك} ؛ أي : وشرع لكم الذي أوحينا إلى محمد عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r5.claim: The shift from tawṣiya to revelation explicitly affirms Muhammad's messengership against deniers; the majestic We signals special care, and his revelation is placed first despite later chronology.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r5.anchor: وتغيير التوصية إلى الإيحاء في جانب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للتصريح برسالته القامع لإنكار الكفرة ، والالتفات إلى نون العظمة لإظهار كمال الاعتناء بإيحائه

BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r6.claim: The relative pronoun al-ladhī conveys exaltation; direct, shifting address honors Muhammad and signals that God instituted the law through him.
BURSEVI:v8p226#3/r6.anchor: والتعبير بالأصل في الموصولات ، وهو الذي للتعظيم وتوجيه الخطاب إليه عليه السلام بطريق التلوين للتشريف

BURSEVI:v8p227/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r1.claim: These five are singled out as the greatest and most famous messengers, possessors of resolve, major revealed laws, and many followers.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r1.anchor: وجه تخصيص هؤلاء الخمسة بالذكر ، أنهم أكابر الأنبياء ومشاهيرهم من أولي العزم وأصحاب الشرائع العظيمة

BURSEVI:v8p227/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r2.claim: The phrase may be accusative as an apposition to the object of instituted and its conjunctions, or nominative as a fresh answer explaining the shared command.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r2.anchor: {أن أقيموا الدين} محله النصب على أنه بدل من مفعول شرع ، والمعطوفين عليه

BURSEVI:v8p227/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r3.claim: The shared religion is Islam: God's oneness and obedience, belief in His books, messengers, the Last Day, and all that makes a person a believer.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r3.anchor: هو إقامة الدين ؛ أي : دين الإسلام الذي هو توحيد الله وطاعته

BURSEVI:v8p227/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r4.claim: Establishing religion means keeping its pillars upright and guarding against deviation, or persisting in it and striving for it.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r4.anchor: والمراد : بإقامته تعديل أركانه وحفظه من أن يقع فيه زيغ ، أو المواظبة عليه والتشمر له.

BURSEVI:v8p227/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r5.claim: The prohibition concerns division over religion's foundations, and the address to Muhammad's community makes this a charge for all people.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r5.anchor: {ولا تتفرقوا فيه} في الدين الذي هو عبارة عن الأصول والخطاب متوجه إلى أمته عليه السلام ، فهذه وصية لجميع العباد.

BURSEVI:v8p227/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r6.claim: The prophets agreed on religion's core and all upheld and preached it: 3:19 affirms Islam without distinction between prophets, while 5:48 allows differing subsidiary laws for communities and temperaments.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r6.anchor: قال الله تعالى : {إن الدين عند الله الإسلام} (آل عمران : 19) من غير تفرقة بين نبي ونبي ومختلفون في الفروع والأحكام. قال تعالى : {لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا}

BURSEVI:v8p227/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r7.claim: God commands unity in establishing religion because divine support is with the group and the wolf takes the sheep that strays from it.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r7.anchor: ثم أمر عباده بإقامة الدين والاجتماع عليه ونهاهم عن التفرق فيه ، فإن يد الله ونصرته مع الجماعة ، وإنما يأكل الذئب الشاة البعيدة

BURSEVI:v8p227/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227/r8.claim: A wise man teaches his sons that a bundled set of sticks cannot be broken but separate sticks can; likewise unity prevents defeat, while division lets enemies overcome the community.
BURSEVI:v8p227/r8.anchor: أوصى حكيم أولاده عند موته ، وكانوا جماعة ، فقال لهم : ائتوني بعصى ، فجمعها ، فقال لهم : اكسروها ، وهي مجموعة ، فلم يقدروا على ذلك

BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r1.claim: The call is great and difficult for the polytheists: Muhammad summons them to monotheism and rejection of idol worship, which they deem astonishing.
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r1.anchor: {كبر على المشركين} ؛ أي : عظم وشق عليهم {ما تدعوهم إليه} يا محمد من التوحيد ورفض عبادة الأصنام

BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says the testimony that none is god but God alone troubled Iblīs and his troops, but God insists on making it prevail over its opponents.
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة : شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده ، ضاق بها إبليس وجنوده ، فأبى الله إلا أن يظهرها على من ناوأها

BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib connects ijtabā to gathering water in a basin called jābiya and to gathering revenue; the root suggests collecting.
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : جبيت الماء في الحوض جمعته والحوض الجامع له جابية ، ومنه استعير جبيت الخراج جباية.

BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r4.claim: Ijtibāʾ is gathering by selection; here the sense of gathering suits the warning against division, while ṣafāʾ alone needs an added sense to take ilā.
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r4.anchor: والاجتباء : الجمع على طريق الاصطفاء ، وهو هنا مأخوذ من الجباية

BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r5.claim: God draws to the call whomever He wills to draw, namely the person who directs their choice toward what is being called to.
BURSEVI:v8p227#3/r5.anchor: والمعنى : الله يجتلب إلى ما تدعوهم إليه من يشاء أن يجتلبه إليه ، وهو من صرف اختياره إلى ما دعي إليه.

BURSEVI:v8p228/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r1.claim: Guidance to God comes by direction, enabling, and the provision of subtle graces; ināba means turning toward Him.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r1.anchor: {ويهدي إليه} بالإرشاد والتوفيق وإمداد الالطاف. {من ينيب} يقبل إليه

BURSEVI:v8p228/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r2.claim: The pronoun in both clauses may refer to what the Prophet calls people toward: God gathers to His presence by selection according to readiness and guides those who turn by providential care.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضميرفي كلا الموضعين ، فالمعنى : الله يجمع إلى جنابه على طريق الاصطفاء من يشاء من عباده بحسب استعداده

BURSEVI:v8p228/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r3.claim: Divine election is a special assignment through an overflowing divine gift that brings many blessings without the servant's effort; it is for prophets and some near them among the truthful and martyrs.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r3.anchor: واجتباء الله تعالى العبد تخصصه إياه بفيض إلهي يتحصل منه أنواع من النعم ، بلا سعي من العبد ، وذلك للأنبياء عليهم السلام

BURSEVI:v8p228/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p228/r4.claim: Al-Kāshifī says whoever turns away from all else and seeks the Real will be shown the way by God.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يعني هركه از همه اعراض كند وحق راخواهد

BURSEVI:v8p228/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p228/r5.claim: The verse signifies the attracted elect, chosen eternally and drawn from both worlds by a divine attraction, and ordinary seekers guided through effort and turning along the path of right guidance.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير بقوله الله يجتبي إليه الآية إلى مقامي المجذوب والسالك

BURSEVI:v8p228/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r6.claim: Ināba results from repentance: when repentance is sound, the person turns toward God.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r6.anchor: والإنابة : نتيجة التوبة فإذا صحت التوبة حصلت الإنابة إلى الله تعالى.

BURSEVI:v8p228/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r7.claim: A Sufi master describes stages of divine guidance: establishing religion at law and nature leads through the path and self, knowledge and spirit, then reality and the secret, culminating in perfected knowing and witnessing; 29:69 is cited.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r7.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من جاهد في إقامة الدين في مقام الشريعة والطبيعة يهديه الله إلى إقامته في مقام الطريقة والنفس

BURSEVI:v8p228/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p228/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p228/r8.claim: Strive to perform every possible act of devotion in every condition; faith that a sin is sinful is itself a strong act of devotion, strengthened by repentance and seeking forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v8p228/r8.anchor: فعليك بإتيان جميع القرب قدر الاستطاعة في كل زمان وحال ، فإن المؤمن لن تخلص له معصية أبدا من غير أن تخالطها طاعة ؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r1.claim: The verse names Noah, the first messenger after Adam, and Muhammad, the last, with Abraham, Moses and Jesus between them as the messengers of firm resolve; their list also appears in 33:7.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r1.anchor: نوح، عليه السلام وآخرهم وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r2.claim: All messengers brought the same religion: worship God alone; the Prophet’s saying that prophets share one religion expresses that common core, though their laws and ways differ, as 5:48 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r2.anchor: والدين الذي جاءت به الرسل كلهم هو: عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، كما قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r3.claim: God enjoined all the prophets to uphold religion together and in accord, and forbade division and disagreement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p194#2/r3.anchor: أي: وصى الله [سبحانه و] (2) تعالى جميع الأنبياء، عليهم السلام، بالائتلاف والجماعة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r1.claim: The call to monotheism is difficult for the polytheists, who reject it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r1.anchor: أي: شق عليهم وأنكروا ما تدعوهم إليه يا محمد من التوحيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r2.claim: God grants guidance to those who merit it and decrees misguidance for those who choose it over the path of right guidance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p195/r2.anchor: هو الذي يقدر الهداية لمن يستحقها، ويكتب الضلالة على من آثرها على طريق الرشد؛

JISHUMI:v9p6223/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r6.claim: Sharʿa and sharīʿa are alike: a manifest, straight doctrine; related verbs mean to establish, enter, make clear, or display.
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r6.anchor: والشرعة والشريعة سواء، وهو: [الظاهر المستقيم] من المذاهب، يقال: شرع الله هذا، أي: جعله مذهبا ظاهرا

JISHUMI:v9p6223/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r7.claim: Ijtibāʾ, iṣṭifāʾ, and ikhtiyār are synonymous terms for selection.

JISHUMI:v9p6223/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r8.claim: Aqīmū al-dīn can be accusative as an appositive to mā in “what He enjoined.”
JISHUMI:v9p6223/r8.anchor: و (أقيموا الدين) يجوز في موضعه ثلاثة أوجه: الأول: النصب على البدل من (ما) في قوله: ما وصى.

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r1.claim: Aqīmū al-dīn can be genitive as an appositive to the pronoun in bihi, or nominative as a new clause.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r1.anchor: الثاني: الجر على البدل من الهاء في قوله: به. الثالث: الرفع على الاستئناف.

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r3.claim: “Do not divide over it” completes a clause; kabura begins anew, though a past verb cannot be raised as proposed.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r3.anchor: (ولا تتفرقوا) تم الكلام، ثم استأنف فقال: (كبر) إلا أن كبر فعل ماض، فهو لا يرتفع.

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r23.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r23.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains sharaʿa lakum as prescribing religion.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r23.anchor: شرع لكم قيل: فرض من الدين، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r24.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r24.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains it as making religion clear and laying it out.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r24.anchor: وقيل: بين لكم ونهج، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r25.claim: What God enjoined is what He commanded the prophets, or prescribed as worship for His prophets.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r25.anchor: ما وصى به أي: أمر الأنبياء به، وقيل: شرع لعباده من الدين ما تعبد به أنبياءه

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r26.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r26.claim: The author prefers interpreting religion as unity of God and justice, which do not vary across revealed laws.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r26.anchor: قيل: التوحيد والعدل، فإن ذلك لا يختلف بالشرائع

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r27.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r27.claim: Another view takes religion to mean the prophets' laws, which may differ but are equally beneficial.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r27.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الشرائع، وأن شرائع الأنبياء مع اختلافها سواء في كونها مصلحة

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r28.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r28.claim: Qatāda interprets it as forbidding the lawful and permitting the unlawful.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r28.anchor: وقيل: أراد تحريم الحلال وتحليل الحرام، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r29.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r29.claim: Another view refers to prohibiting marriage to mothers, sisters, and daughters.

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r30.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r30.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid include professing God, obedience, worship, gratitude, prayer, and almsgiving.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r30.anchor: وقيل: هو الإقرار بالله، والطاعة له، والقيام بعبادته وشكره علي نعمه، وإقام الصلاة، وإيتاء الزكاة، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r31.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r31.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r31.claim: Religion may refer to the command itself: establish it, hold to the community, and avoid division.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r31.anchor: وقيل: هو قوله: (أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه)، فبعث الأنبياء بإقامة الدين، والتمسك بالجماعة، وترك المفارقة والمخالفة

JISHUMI:v9p6224/r32.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r32.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r32.claim: “What He enjoined” emphasizes the strong charge to preserve and adhere to it.
JISHUMI:v9p6224/r32.anchor: (ما وصى) أي: بالغ في الوصية في حفظه والتمسك

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r1.claim: One construction repeats “He prescribed”: what He prescribed for Noah, and what He revealed to Muḥammad.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r1.anchor: قيل: تقديره شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا، وشرع ما أوحينا إليك

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r2.claim: Another construction coordinates what was revealed to Muḥammad with what was enjoined for Noah.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r2.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: ما وصى به نوحا وبالذي أوحينا إليك، ثم فسر ذلك فقال

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r3.claim: Establishing religion means believing it and acting on it.

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r4.claim: One view forbids believers from declaring one another unbelievers or misguided and calls them to unity and evidence for truth.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r4.anchor: قيل: لا يكفر بعضكم بعضا ولا يضلل، ولكن عليكم بالألفة والجماعة، والتمسك بالأدلة المؤدية إلى الحق

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r5.claim: Unity on truth comes from examining evidence and abandoning imitation, desire, and following ambiguities.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r5.anchor: قلنا: بالنظر في الأدلة، وترك التقليد والهوى واتباع الشبه.

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r6.claim: Another view forbids sects from fragmenting religion into competing beliefs, since truth is one.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r6.anchor: وقيل: لا تتفرقوا في الدين فتعتقد كل طائفة شيئا، فإن الحق في واحد.

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r7.claim: The call to God's oneness and rejection of rivals is difficult for the polytheists.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r7.anchor: (كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه) أي: عظم عليهم ما دعوتهم إليه من توحيد الله، وخلع الأنداد

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r8.claim: It may be hard for them to leave disbelief because they are attached to their ancestors' religion.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r8.anchor: وقيل: شق عليهم مفارقة الكفر؛ لإلفهم دين آبائهم

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r9.claim: Another explanation is that monotheism threatens their leadership.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r9.anchor: وقيل: عظم عليهم ذلك؛ لما فيه من زوال رئاستهم

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r10.claim: The author prefers the view that they found it difficult to follow Muḥammad's commands about religion.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r10.anchor: وقيل: شق عليهم اتباعك فيما تأمرهم به من الدين، وهذا هو الوجه

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r11.claim: Selection belongs to God, not people: He chooses whom He wills for prophethood.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r11.anchor: الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء أي: ليس إليهم الاختيار؛ لأن الله يجتبي لرسالته من يشاء

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r12.claim: The preposition ilā may mean li, so the phrase means choosing someone for the prophetic mission.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r12.anchor: وقيل: إلى بمعنى اللام، أي: يجتبي لرسالته من يشاء

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r13.claim: Abū Muslim explains the phrase as God accepting whomever He wills.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r13.anchor: وقيل: يتقبل ممن يشاء، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r14.claim: One view explains guidance as God's gentle assistance (luṭf).

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r15.claim: Another view says God raises a person in worldly rank through prophethood and guides him.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r15.anchor: وقيل: يرفع درجته في الدنيا بالرسالة ويهديه

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r16.claim: A further view says God guides accountable people to His religion and the right path.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r16.anchor: وقيل: يهدي إلى دينه وطريق الحق، وهم المكلفون

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r17.claim: Another view takes the destination as the path to Paradise and reward.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r17.anchor: وقيل: يهديه إلى طريق الجنة والثواب

JISHUMI:v9p6227/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r18.claim: Ināba means returning to God in sincere devotion.
JISHUMI:v9p6227/r18.anchor: وينيب قيل: يرجع إلى ربه في إخلاص دينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r1.claim: God prescribed for this community the religion of Noah, Muḥammad, and the prophets between them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r1.anchor: دين نوح ومحمد ومن بينهما من الأنبياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r2.claim: The shared prescription is to uphold Islam: God’s oneness and obedience, belief in messengers and scriptures, the Day of Judgment, and what makes a person Muslim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r2.anchor: إقامة دين الإسلام الذي هو توحيد الله وطاعته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r3.claim: The common command concerns Islam’s fundamentals, not separate laws tailored to different communities and circumstances (5:48).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r3.anchor: الشرائع التي هي مصالح الأمم على حسب أحوالها ، فإنها مختلفة متفاوتة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r4.claim: The clause to uphold the religion may be accusative as an appositive to the object of prescribed, or nominative as a new explanation of what was prescribed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r4.anchor: { أن أقيموا } إما نصب بدل من مفعول شرع والمعطوفين عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r5.claim: He illustrates the explanatory resumption with the parallel formulation at 21:92.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى : { إن هاذه أمتكم * أمة واحدة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r6.claim: It is great upon the associators means establishing God’s religion is weighty and difficult for them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r6.anchor: كبر على المشركين } عظم عليهم وشق عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r7.claim: Yajtabī means to draw and gather toward the religion; God does so by enabling and supporting those who benefit from His guidance and receive His gentleness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p219#2/r7.anchor: الضمير للدين بالتوفيق والتسديد { من يشاء } من ينفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r1.claim: One sense is that God instituted something for you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r1.anchor: وفي { شرع لكم } أربعة أوجه : أحدها : سن لكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r2.claim: Another sense is that God made it clear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r2.anchor: الثاني : بين لكم . الثالث : اختار لكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means God chose it for you.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r4.claim: A fourth sense is that God made it obligatory.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r5.claim: The phrase means “the religion”; من is redundant here.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r5.anchor: يعني الدين ومن زائدة في الكلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r6.speaker: الحكم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r6.claim: Al-Hakam says Noah first brought the prohibition of marrying mothers, daughters, and sisters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r6.anchor: لأنه أول نبي أتى أمته بتحريم . ذلك ، قاله الحكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r7.claim: Qatada says it means permitting the lawful and forbidding the unlawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r7.anchor: الثاني : تحليل الحلال وتحريم الحرام , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r8.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says it means acting according to the religion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r9.claim: Another view is calling people to the religion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r10.claim: Mujahid says God's religion is one: obedience and monotheism.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد : دين الله في طاعته وتوحيده واحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r11.claim: A further possibility is striving against opponents of the religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r11.anchor: ويحتمل وجها ثالثا : جاهدوا عليه من عانده

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r12.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says not to become enemies over it but to be brothers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r12.anchor: أحدهما : لا تتعادوا عليه , وكونوا عليه إخوانا , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r13.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r13.claim: Muqatil says not to differ, since each prophet confirms the previous one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r13.anchor: الثانية : لا تختلفوا فيه فإن كل نبي مصدق لمن قبله , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r14.claim: Qatada says the difficult call is the testimony that no god exists but God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r14.anchor: قاله قتادة : من شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r15.claim: Another possibility is recognition of the Prophet's messengership, harder and more repellent to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r15.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من الاعتراف بنبوته , لأنه عليهم أشد وهم منه أنفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r16.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r16.claim: Al-Kalbi says God selects those born Muslim and guides those entering Islam from shirk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r16.anchor: هو من يسلم من الشرك , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r17.claim: Mujahid says God selects or draws near whomever He wills.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r17.anchor: الثاني : يستخلص إليه من يشاء . قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r18.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r18.claim: Al-Suddi says God guides those who turn toward obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p196/r18.anchor: ويهدي إليه من يقبل على طاعته , قاله السدي

MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says God enjoined Muhammad and all the prophets to follow Islam as one religion.
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ﴾ يقول أوصاك به يا محمد وأنبياءه كلهم بالإسلام دينا واحدا

MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r2.claim: Mujahid explains God's choosing whom He wills as selecting that person for Himself.
MUJAHID:v2p573#4/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ يجتبي إليه من يشاء ﴾ قال يقول الله عز وجل يستخلص لنفسه من يشاء

MUQATIL:42:13/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r1.claim: “He prescribed for you” means He made religion clear; another explanation is that He established Islam’s precedents, and min is an extra particle.
MUQATIL:42:13/r1.anchor: يقول: بين لكم، ويقال: سن لكم آثار الإسلام

MUQATIL:42:13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r2.claim: There is fronting: the enjoinder to Noah and revelation to Muhammad precede the enjoinder to Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, followed by the command to establish religion.
MUQATIL:42:13/r2.anchor: فيه تقديم، { وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين }

MUQATIL:42:13/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r3.claim: Establishing the religion means affirming monotheism.

MUQATIL:42:13/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r4.claim: The command not to divide in religion was difficult for Meccan polytheists because Muhammad called them to monotheism, as in their objection at 38:5.
MUQATIL:42:13/r4.anchor: كبر على المشركين } يقول: عظم على مشركى مكة، { ما تدعوهم إليه

MUQATIL:42:13/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r5.claim: God chooses and draws people to His religion.
MUQATIL:42:13/r5.anchor: الله يجتبي إليه } ، يقول: يستخلص لدينه

MUQATIL:42:13/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:13/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:13/r6.claim: God guides to His religion those who turn back in repentance.
MUQATIL:42:13/r6.anchor: إلى دينه، { من ينيب } [آية: 13]، يعنى من يراجع التوبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r1.claim: Sharaʿa means He explained and made clear.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ شرع ﴾ بين واظهر ﴿ لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r2.claim: God prescribed the religion of Noah and Muhammad and that of the prophets between them; their shared charge is then stated as establishing the religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r2.anchor: اى شرع لكم من الدين دين نوح ومحمد وما بينهما من الانبياء عليهم السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r3.claim: Establishing the religion means Islam: God's oneness and obedience, belief in His messengers and books, the Day of Judgment, and all that makes one Muslim; distinct legal codes varied among prophets.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r3.anchor: والمراد اقامة دين الاسلام الذى هو توحيد الله وطاعته والايمان برسله وكتبه وبيوم الجزاء وسائر ما يكون المرء باقامته مسلما

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r4.claim: An aqīmū is accusative as an appositive to the object of sharaʿa and its coordinated objects, or nominative as an independent explanation of what was prescribed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r4.anchor: ومحل ان اقيموا نصب بدل من مفعول شرع والمعطوفين عليه أو رفع على الاستئناف كانه قيل وما ذلك المشروع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r5.claim: It means do not disagree about the religion.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r6.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r6.claim: ʿAlī says unity is mercy and division is torment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r6.anchor: قال علي رضى الله عنه لا تتفرقوا فالجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r7.claim: Establishing God's religion and affirming His oneness is great and difficult for the polytheists.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ كبر على المشركين ﴾ عظم عليهم وشق عليهم ﴿ ما تدعوهم إليه ﴾ من اقامة دين الله والتوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r8.claim: Yajtibī means He draws and gathers people to the religion through enabling help; He guides those who turn toward obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p98#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ الله يجتبي ﴾ يجلب ويجمع ﴿ إليه ﴾ إلى الدين بالتوفيق والتسديد

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r1.claim: Establishing religion means affirming God's oneness, obeying Him, believing His messengers, books and final recompense, and practicing what makes a person Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r1.anchor: وهو توحيد الله وطاعته، والإيمان برسله وكتبه وبيوم الجزاء، وبسائر ما يكون الرجل بإقامته مسلما

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r2.claim: The root means to lay out and clarify a path, or institute a rule; related usages include a main road, access to water, stripping hide, splitting, and entering an undertaking.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r2.anchor: ومعنى «شرع» أي نهج وأوضح وبين المسالك. وقد شرع لهم يشرع شرعا أي سن

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r3.claim: One parsing makes أن nominative as the subject of an implied الذي وصى به نوحا; on this reading, one pauses at عيسى.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r3.anchor: «أن» في محل رفع، على تقدير والذي وصى به نوحا أن أقيموا الدين، ويوقف على هذا الوجه على «عيسى»

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r4.claim: A second parsing makes أن accusative: God prescribed establishing the religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو نصب، أي شرع لكم إقامة الدين. وقيل: هو جر بدلا من الهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r5.claim: A third parsing makes أن a genitive substitute for the pronoun in به, as if it said to establish the religion through it; there is no pause at عيسى.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو جر بدلا من الهاء في «به» كأنه قال: به أقيموا الدين. ولا يوقف على «عيسى» على هذين الوجهين

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r6.claim: Alternatively, أن is explanatory, like أن امشوا, and has no grammatical case.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون «أن» مفسرة مثل: أن امشوا، فلا يكون لها محل من الإعراب.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r7.claim: In the sound, famous intercession report, the Prophet identifies Noah as the first messenger God sent to the people of earth; al-Qurtubi calls the report sound and unproblematic.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r7.anchor: ثبت في الحديث الصحيح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في حديث الشفاعة الكبير المشهور

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r8.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Adam was the first prophet, without imposed duties or prohibitions, while Noah brought prohibitions, obligations and religious manners; successive prophets reinforced these until Muhammad completed the best religious community.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r8.anchor: كما أن آدم أول نبي بغير إشكال لأن آدم لم يكن معه إلا نبوة، ولم تفرض له الفرائض

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r9.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the prophets shared one religion in fundamentals: monotheism, worship, honesty, fidelity, trust, kinship, and prohibitions on disbelief, murder, adultery, harming people or animals, and disgraceful conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r9.anchor: فكان المعنى أوصيناك يا محمد ونوحا دينا واحدا يعني في الأصول التي لا تختلف فيها الشريعة

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r10.claim: Establish the shared religion continuously, preserving it without disagreement or instability; particular laws differed across peoples and times according to divine wisdom and their interests.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14/r10.anchor: أي اجعلوه قائما يريد دائما مستمرا محفوظا مستقرا من غير خلاف فيه ولا اضطراب

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r1.claim: Whoever breaks faith harms himself, as stated in the verse about whoever breaks his pledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r1.anchor: فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r2.claim: Mujahid, al-Walibi transmitting from Ibn Abbas, and al-Kalbi say every prophet was charged with prayer, almsgiving and obedience to God; this is the religion prescribed to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: لم يبعث الله نبيا قط إلا وصاه بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والإقرار لله بالطاعة، فذلك دينه الذي شرع لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r3.claim: Qatada interprets the shared religion as declaring lawful what God made lawful and unlawful what He made unlawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني تحليل الحلال وتحريم الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r4.speaker: الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r4.claim: Al-Hakam says the common prescription included prohibiting mothers, sisters and daughters in marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r4.anchor: وقال الحكم: تحريم الأمهات والأخوات والبنات

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r5.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr's account gathers the preceding interpretations and adds further shared religious fundamentals.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r5.anchor: وما ذكره القاضي يجمع هذه الأقوال ويزيد عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r6.claim: Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus are singled out because they were principal bearers of revealed law.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r6.anchor: وخص نوحا وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى بالذكر لأنهم أرباب الشرائع

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r7.claim: What the polytheists find burdensome is the call to monotheism and rejection of idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r7.anchor: { ما تدعوهم إليه } من التوحيد ورفض الأوثان

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the confession that there is no god but God weighed heavily on polytheists and distressed Satan and his troops, but God would support and raise it over its opponents.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: كبر على المشركين فاشتد عليهم شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وضاق بها إبليس وجنوده

QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r9.claim: God chooses whom He wills for monotheism and draws into His religion those who turn back to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:13-14#2/r9.anchor: أي يختار. والاجتباء الاختيار أي يختار للتوحيد من يشاء. { ويهدي إليه من ينيب } أي يستخلص لدينه من رجع إليه.

QASHANI:42:13/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:42:13/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:42:13/r1.claim: The universal religion prescribed to all prophets is the common foundation they must establish without division: monotheism, justice, and belief in God and the afterlife.
QASHANI:42:13/r1.anchor: المطلق الذي وصى جميع الأنبياء بإقامته واجتماعهم عليه وعدم تفرقهم فيه

QASHANI:42:13/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:42:13/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:42:13/r2.claim: The shared religion concerns unchanging knowledge and deeds, while differing revealed laws concern changing practices, worship, and transactions, as 5:48 says each community has a law and a way.
QASHANI:42:13/r2.anchor: فالدين القيم هو المتعلق بما لا يتغير من العلوم والأعمال، والشريعة هي المتعلقة بما يتغير

QASHANI:42:13/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:42:13/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:42:13/r3.claim: Monotheism weighs heavily on polytheists because they are veiled by attachment to other-than-God and stand among manifestations of wrath, not the beloved or those guided to turn toward God.
QASHANI:42:13/r3.anchor: المحجوبين عن الحق بالغير { ما تدعوهم إليه } من التوحيد لكونهم أهل المقت

QASHANI:42:13/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:42:13/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:42:13/r4.claim: God draws the beloved to Him before spiritual discipline through prior election; those who love Him are enabled to turn through wayfaring, effort, longing, and need, then guided by His light and beauty.
QASHANI:42:13/r4.anchor: المحبوبين الذين اجتباهم الله بمحض عنايته ومجرد مشيئته ولا من المحبين

QASHANI:42:13/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:42:13/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:42:13/r5.claim: Those veiled from God are expelled from His door and distanced from His presence by a prior decree of wretchedness.
QASHANI:42:13/r5.anchor: وطرد المحجوبين عن بابه وأبعدهم عن جنابه بسابقة كلمة القضاء عليهم بالشقاء

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r1.claim: After 42:3 exalts revelation to Muhammad and earlier prophets, this verse details that shared divine legislation.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r1.anchor: لما عظم وحيه إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله { كذلك يوحى إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r2.claim: God prescribed Muhammad's community the religion He enjoined on Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r2.anchor: شرع الله لكم يا أصحاب محمد من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ومحمدا وآبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r3.claim: These five are singled out because they are the leading prophets, bearers of great laws, and followed by many.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r3.anchor: لأنهم أكابر الأنبياء وأصحاب الشرائع العظيمة والأتباع الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r4.claim: Razi flags the differing formulas for Noah, Muhammad, and Abraham as a textual problem requiring explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r4.anchor: أنه قال في أول الآية { ما وصى به نوحا } وفي آخرها { وما وصينا به إبراهيم } وفي الوسط { والذى أوحينا إليك } فما الفائدة

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r5.claim: He also asks why Noah is described in the third person while the references to Muhammad and Abraham use the first person.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r5.anchor: أنه ذكر نوحا عليه السلام على سبيل الغيبة فقال : { ما وصى به نوحا } والقسمين الباقيين على سبيل التكلم

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r6.claim: A further difficulty is the apparent shift from third-person address in “He prescribed” to direct address in “We revealed to you” within one construction.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r6.anchor: فهذا يقتضي الجمع بين خطاب الغيبة وخطاب الحضور في الكلام الواحد بالاعتبار الواحد

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r7.claim: The common religion means unchanging beliefs in God, angels, books, messengers, and the Last Day, not legal rules that vary by community; it calls for turning from worldly life, seeking the afterlife, virtue, and avoiding vice.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r7.anchor: الأمور التي لا تختلف باختلاف الشرائع / وهي الإيمان بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r8.claim: Razi proposes that the prohibition on division may mean rejecting numerous gods, as Joseph calls people divided among gods inferior to worshipping the One, and messengers preach that there is no god but God.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r8.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يكون المراد من قوله { ولا تتفرقوا } أي لا تتفرقوا بالآلهة الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r9.claim: Some infer that Muhammad initially followed Noah's law; Razi rejects this, since the verse also names other prophets and points to the law agreed upon by them all.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r9.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بقوله { شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا } على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r10.claim: The command to establish religion can be parsed as an accusative substitute for the object of “prescribed” and its coordinated clauses, or as a nominative resumption answering what was prescribed.

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r11.claim: The call to establish God's religion in agreement and unanimity was grave and difficult for the polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r11.anchor: عظم عليهم وشق عليهم { ما تدعوهم إليه } من إقامة دين الله تعالى على سبيل الاتفاق والإجماع

RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r12.claim: The polytheists' complaint that Muhammad would make many gods into one illustrates why this call was hard for them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p134/r12.anchor: بدليل أن الكفار قالوا { أجعل الالهة إلاها واحدا إن هاذا لشىء عجاب }

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r1.speaker: نفاة القياس
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r1.claim: Opponents of analogical reasoning argue that the command to establish one religion without division forbids qiyas, since it opens the door to disputes and schools based on it remain divided through the end of time.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r1.anchor: احتج نفاة القياس بهذه الآية قالوا إنه تعالى أخبر أن أكابر الأنبياء أطبقوا على أنه يجب إقامة الدين بحث لا يفضي إلى الاختلاف والتنازع

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r2.claim: Religious prescriptions include permanent principles that cannot be abrogated, such as truthfulness, justice, and beneficence, and variable rules that differ among religions, such as prohibitions of lying, oppression, and harm.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r2.anchor: منها ما يمتنع دخول النسخ والتغيير فيه ، بل يكون واجب البقاء في جميع الشرائع والأديان

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r3.claim: The law gives stronger emphasis to the permanent moral principles because observing them cultivates states that bring happiness in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r3.anchor: ودلت هذه الآية على أن سعي الشرع في تقرير النوع الأول أقوى من سعيه في تقرير النوع الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r4.claim: Agreement is valued by both reason and revelation because aligned souls strengthen one another's influence.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r4.anchor: أن للنفوس تأثيرات ، وإذا تطابقت النفوس وتوافقت على واحد قوي التأثير

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r5.claim: Agreement lets each person assist the others toward a shared aim, and more helpers make success more likely.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r5.anchor: أنها إذا توافقت صار كل واحد منها معينا للآخر في ذلك المقصود المعين ، وكثرة الأعوان توجب حصول المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r6.claim: Disagreement undermines the world's welfare by producing disorder, killing, and plunder; the same principle appears in the prohibition on contention in 8:46.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135/r6.anchor: حصول التنازع ضد مصلحة العالم لأن ذلك يفضي إلى الهرج والمرج والقتل والنهب

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r1.claim: One reading is that God directed Muhammad's community to the shared religion because He chose them and singled them out for added mercy and honor.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r1.anchor: إلى التمسك بالدين المتفق عليه بين أنه تعالى إنما أرشدهم إلى هذا الخير ، لأنه اجتباهم واصطفاهم

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r2.claim: Another reading is that the messengers' call was hard for the polytheists because obedience to them wounded their pride; God chooses messengers regardless of rank, lineage, or wealth, and people must follow them.

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r3.claim: Ijtabā derives from gathering and drawing something together, as in collecting revenue or gathering water in a basin; God's choosing means drawing someone near with honor and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r3.anchor: واشتقاق لفظ الاجتباء يدل على الضم والجمع ، فمنه جبي الخراج واجتباه وجبى الماء في الحوض

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r4.claim: The wording “whomever He wills” follows the pattern of 29:21, where God says He punishes and shows mercy to whomever He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r4.anchor: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r5.claim: A reported divine saying promises that whoever approaches God by obedience receives God's approach through guidance, the opening of the heart, and ease in affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r5.anchor: الخبر ( من تقرب مني شبرا تقربت منه ذراعا ومن أتاني يمشي أتيته هرولة )

RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r6.claim: Turning to God brings His guidance and direction: He opens the servant's heart and makes the path easier.
RAZI-FULL:v27p135#2/r6.anchor: من أقبل إلي بطاعته أقبلت إليه بهدايتي وإرشادي بأن أشرح له صدره وأسهل أمره

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r1.claim: The opening resembles 4:163–64; the Quran's treatment of revelation's universality is discussed in the essay on sacred history and other religions.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r1.anchor: The first part of this verse is similar to 4:163–64

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r2.claim: Upholding religion means acting in accord with it, or holding fast, fulfilling its obligations, remaining faithful, and calling others to it.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r2.anchor: To uphold religion means that to act in accord with it (Ṭ) or to hold fast to it, perform its obligations

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r3.claim: Avoiding division means not repeating earlier religious communities' sectarianism, but remaining united as brothers.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r3.anchor: to not be like earlier religious communities that divided into sects (Ṭ), but rather to remain united in religion as brothers (Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r4.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says division is destruction, while unity is something upon which one can rely.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r4.anchor: al-Ṭabarī says that division is destruction and being unified is something upon which one can rely

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r5.claim: The call is grievous to idolaters because it undermines their religion and because they envy Muhammad for receiving revelation instead of someone else.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r5.anchor: The Prophet’s call to belief in Divine Unity and sincere devotion to God is grievous for the idolaters both because it undermines their religion

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r6.claim: The antecedent of the pronoun rendered “Himself” is uncertain; the sentence can instead read that God chooses and guides whomever He wills “for it,” meaning religion or bearing witness to Divine Unity.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r6.anchor: The antecedent of the pronoun here rendered Himself is not completely clear. The sentence could also be read

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r7.claim: God's guidance of whoever turns in repentance evokes a sacred report about God drawing nearer to the servant who draws near to Him.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r7.anchor: That God guides whosoever turns in repentance (cf. 13:27) evokes the famous ḥadīth qudsī

STUDYQURAN:42:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r8.speaker: ḥadīth qudsī
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r8.claim: The sacred report says God responds to a servant's approach by drawing nearer, and comes running when the servant comes walking.
STUDYQURAN:42:13/r8.anchor: if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running

QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r18.claim: Shara'a means to clarify and make manifest.

QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r19.claim: The shared religion means its foundations, while branches differ; the verse also indicates that some legal rulings are common to all revealed laws.
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r19.anchor: أراد به أصول الدين ؛ فإنها لا تختلف

QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r20.claim: The command to establish religion and avoid division clarifies the shared fundamentals across prophetic laws.
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r20.anchor: ثم بين ذلك بقوله : { أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه }

QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r21.claim: A narrative says the prohibition of marrying daughters and sisters was instituted in Noah's time.
QUSHAYRI:v3p159/r21.anchor: وفي القصة أن تحريم البنات والأخوات إنما شرع في زمان نوح

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r1.claim: God prescribed for people the religion He enjoined Noah to practice, the revelation He gave Muhammad, and what He enjoined Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r1.anchor: الناس {من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} [الشورى: 13] أن يعمله

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r2.claim: He allows three parses for أن أقيموا: accusative as an explication of ما, genitive as an explanation of the pronoun in به, or nominative as an independent clause meaning the prescribed religion is to establish it.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون في موضع خفض ردا على الهاء التي في قوله: {به} [البقرة: 22] وتفسيرا عنها

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r3.claim: The prophets shared one injunction: establish the true religion and do not divide over it.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r3.anchor: فمعلوم أن الذي أوصى به جميع هؤلاء الأنبياء وصية واحدة، وهي إقامة الدين الحق، ولا تتفرقوا فيه

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says what Noah was enjoined, and what all the prophets were enjoined, was one religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ما وصى به نوحا} [الشورى: 13] قال: «ما أوصاك به وأنبياءه كلهم دين واحد»

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the prescribed religion as the whole religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} [الشورى: 13] قال: «هو الدين كله»

TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r6.claim: Qatāda describes Noah’s message as a law that makes the lawful lawful and the forbidden forbidden; another report summarizes it as halal and haram.
TAB-FULL:v20p479#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} [الشورى: 13] «بعث نوح حين بعث بالشريعة بتحليل الحلال، وتحريم الحرام»

TAB-FULL:v20p481/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that what was said to the Prophet is sufficient for him.
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا} [الشورى: 13] إلى آخر الآية قال: «حسبك ما قيل لك»

TAB-FULL:v20p481/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r2.claim: Establishing the religion means acting according to what God legislated and prescribed, as in the earlier explanation of إقامة الصلاة.
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r2.anchor: أن اعملوا به على ما شرع لكم وفرض، كما قد بينا فيما مضى قبل في قوله: {أقيموا الصلاة}

TAB-FULL:v20p481/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains the command to establish the religion as a command to act by it.
TAB-FULL:v20p481/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {أن أقيموا، الدين} [الشورى: 13] قال: «اعملوا به»

TAB-FULL:v20p482/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r1.claim: The command forbids disagreement in the religion they were ordered to uphold, as earlier communities had divided.
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تتفرقوا فيه} [الشورى: 13] «تعلموا أن الفرقة هلكة، وأن الجماعة ثقة»

TAB-FULL:v20p482/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r2.claim: Qatāda says people should learn that division brings ruin while unity is security.
TAB-FULL:v20p482/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تتفرقوا فيه} [الشورى: 13] «تعلموا أن الفرقة هلكة، وأن الجماعة ثقة»

TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r1.claim: What burdens the polytheists is Muhammad’s call to worship Allah alone, affirm His exclusive divinity, and disavow other gods and idols.
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه} [الشورى: 13] قال: «أنكرها المشركون، وكبر عليهم شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the polytheists recoiled from the testimony of Allah’s oneness; Satan opposed it, but God made it prevail over its opponents.
TAB-FULL:v20p482#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه} [الشورى: 13] قال: «أنكرها المشركون، وكبر عليهم شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v20p483/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r1.claim: Allah selects whom He wills from creation and chooses for Himself and His guardianship those whom He loves.
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب} [الشورى: 13] يقول: «ويوفق للعمل بطاعته

TAB-FULL:v20p483/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r2.claim: Mujāhid says God enables obedience and following the truth brought by His Prophet for those who turn to obedience and repent from sins.
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب} [الشورى: 13] يقول: «ويوفق للعمل بطاعته

TAB-FULL:v20p483/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says those guided to God are people who turn toward obedience to Him.
TAB-FULL:v20p483/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {ويهدي إليه من ينيب} [الشورى: 13] «من يقبل إلى طاعة الله»

SULAMI:v2p225#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r1.claim: Sahl says Noah first prohibited marriage to mothers, daughters, and sisters; the shared prophetic religion calls for obedience to God, sincerity, and manifesting good character and states.
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : أول من حرم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات نوح عليه السلام فشرع الله لنا محاسن شرائع

SULAMI:v2p225#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r2.claim: Some interpret the ordained religion as the reverence for Muhammad that earlier prophets were commanded to uphold.
SULAMI:v2p225#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ شرع لكم من الدين ﴾ أي من تعظيم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أمر به الأنبياء

TUSTARI:42:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:42:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:42:13/r1.claim: Noah was the first to prohibit daughters, mothers, and sisters in marriage; God prescribed for this community the best aspects of the prophets' laws.
TUSTARI:42:13/r1.anchor: فأول من حرم البنات والأمهات والأخوات نوح عليه السلام، فشرع الله لنا

TUSTARI:42:13/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:42:13/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:42:13/r2.claim: The charge given to Muhammad and the earlier prophets is to establish obedience to God and sincerity in it, and to manifest good character and spiritual states.
TUSTARI:42:13/r2.anchor: من إقامة الطاعة لله وإقامة الإخلاص فيها

TABATABAI:42:13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r1.claim: This passage identifies revelation by its content: the one divine religion, a way of life people should follow toward happiness.
TABATABAI:42:13/r1.anchor: يعرف الوحي الإلهي بأثره الذي هو مفاده وما احتوى عليه من المضمون وهو الدين الإلهي الواحد

TABATABAI:42:13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r2.claim: The context presents Muḥammad’s law as encompassing revealed laws, while divisions arise from human transgression after knowledge, not revelation.
TABATABAI:42:13/r2.anchor: الشريعة المحمدية أجمع الشرائع المنزلة وأن الاختلافات الواقعة في دين الله على وحدته ليست من ناحية الوحي السماوي وإنما هي من بغي الناس

TABATABAI:42:13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r3.claim: The verb sharaʿa, as in ‘he made a road,’ means to make a clear, level path.
TABATABAI:42:13/r3.anchor: يقال شرع الطريق شرعا أي سواه طريقا واضحا بينا

TABATABAI:42:13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:42:13/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a testament as urging another to act with admonition; the related expression for land describes continuous vegetation.
TABATABAI:42:13/r4.anchor: قال الراغب الوصية التقدم إلى الغير بما يعمل مقترنا بوعظ

TABATABAI:42:13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r5.claim: The choice of ‘enjoined’ signals special importance, since one selects matters about which one particularly cares.
TABATABAI:42:13/r5.anchor: وفي معناه إشعار بالأهمية فما كل أمر يوصى به

TABATABAI:42:13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r6.claim: God clarified for the Prophet and his community a religious way of life, including the law entrusted to Noah; the address includes both.
TABATABAI:42:13/r6.anchor: أي بين وأوضح لكم من الدين وهو سنة الحياة

TABATABAI:42:13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r7.claim: The contrast with Noah points to the knowledge and rulings distinctive to Muḥammad’s law; his comprehensive law includes major and minor matters unlike earlier, more limited laws.
TABATABAI:42:13/r7.anchor: ظاهر المقابلة بينه وبين نوح عليه السلام أن المراد بما أوحى إليه

TABATABAI:42:13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r8.claim: The shift to first-person plural in ‘what We revealed’ conveys majesty, as dignitaries speak for themselves and their attendants.
TABATABAI:42:13/r8.anchor: والالتفات في قوله { والذي أوحينا } من الغيبة إلى التكلم

TABATABAI:42:13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r9.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the clause about Noah and means the law prescribed for each of Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
TABATABAI:42:13/r9.anchor: وقوله { وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى } عطف على قوله { وما وصى به }

TABATABAI:42:13/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13/r10.claim: The lawgivers are otherwise named chronologically; Muḥammad is placed first to honor and privilege him.
TABATABAI:42:13/r10.anchor: وإنما قدم ذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للتشريف والتفضيل

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r1.claim: The cited covenant verse likewise places Muḥammad before Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r1.anchor: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r2.claim: Noah is named first to indicate the antiquity and long duration of this law.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r2.anchor: وإنما قدم نوحا وبدأ به للدلالة على قدم هذه الشريعة وطول عهدها

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r3.claim: The tone of divine favor, especially the verse’s ending and next verse, indicates that Muḥammad’s law encompasses earlier laws.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r3.anchor: أن السياق بما أنه يفيد الامتنان وخاصة بالنظر إلى ذيل الآية والآية التالية

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r4.claim: Each community having its own law and path does not rule out a law’s comprehensiveness.

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r5.claim: The divinely revealed laws are those of Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muḥammad; the verse would name any others.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r5.anchor: الشرائع الإلهية المنتسبة إلى الوحي إنما هي شريعة نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ومحمد

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r6.claim: This entails that before Noah there was no social law in the sense of rules governing communities and resolving social conflict.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r6.anchor: أن لا شريعة قبل نوح عليه السلام بمعنى القوانين الحاكمة

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r7.claim: Prophets after Noah followed Noah’s law until Abraham; later prophets followed Abraham’s law until Moses, and so on.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r7.anchor: أن الأنبياء المبعوثين بعد نوح كانوا على شريعته

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r8.claim: The five named prophets are the law-bearing, resolute prophets; the verse would have named any others.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r8.anchor: الأنبياء أصحاب الشرائع وأولي العزم هم هؤلاء الخمسة

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r9.claim: The particle an introduces an explanation of the preceding command to prescribe religion.

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r10.claim: Establishing religion means preserving it through adherence and practice; the definite article refers to this prescribed religion, and avoiding division preserves its unity.

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r11.claim: Everyone must uphold the whole revealed religion together, without fragmenting it by observing some parts and abandoning others.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r11.anchor: محصله أن عليهم جميعا إقامة الدين جميعا وعدم التفرق والتشتت فيه

TABATABAI:42:13#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r12.claim: All revealed laws are one religion that people must establish without division, believing everything revealed and practicing what is binding.
TABATABAI:42:13#2/r12.anchor: فجميع الشرائع التي أنزلها الله على أنبيائه دين واحد يجب إقامته

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r1.claim: An abrogated ruling remains true for its particular people and period; abrogation discloses its end rather than invalidating it.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r1.anchor: فالحكم المنسوخ حق دائما غير أنه خاص بطائفة خاصة في زمن خاص

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r2.claim: People living under a ruling must believe and practice it; later people must believe it was true without practicing it after its term ends.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r2.anchor: يجب عليهم أن يؤمنوا به ويعملوا به

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r3.claim: The command is unrestricted and applies to everyone in every age.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r3.anchor: مطلق شامل لجميع الناس في جميع الأزمان

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r4.speaker: جمع
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r4.claim: Some restrict the command to rulings shared by revealed laws, treating law-specific rules as varying by community; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this limitation.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r4.anchor: فساد قول جمع إن الأمر بالإقامة وعدم التفرق إنما يشمل الأحكام المشتركة

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r5.claim: That restriction would reduce the command to the three fundamentals, since no detailed rule is common in every respect across all laws; this conflicts with the context and cited verses.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r5.anchor: ولو كان كما يقولون كان الأمر بالإقامة مختصا بأصول الدين الثلاثة

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r6.claim: What the Prophet calls the polytheists to is the religion of divine unity, not merely the bare principle of God’s oneness.
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r6.anchor: المراد بقوله { ما تدعوهم إليه } دين التوحيد الذي كان يدعو إليه النبي

TABATABAI:42:13#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:13#3/r7.speaker: author
